# luminous_ui — Project Docs & Continuation System

This `docs/` tree is the **durable memory of the project**. It exists so any new
Claude Code session (or human) can resume work **without reloading the whole
codebase into context**. Read this file first, then load only the docs relevant
to your task.

> **These docs are a guide, not a rulebook.** They capture the current best plan
> and the *reasoning* behind it — not a fixed process to execute blindly. If,
> while working, the code or new context reveals a better or simpler approach,
> **propose it**: say what you'd change and why, and (once it's the direction)
> update the affected doc + record the shift in `decisions.md`. The plans exist
> to be improved, not obeyed. What must be preserved is the *rationale* and the
> *update trail*, so the next session understands why things are the way they are.

## New session? Resume protocol

1. Read **`progress.md`** — the single source of truth for *what's done, what's
   in flight, and where to pick up* (the **Resume point**).
2. Skim **`roadmap.md`** for the big picture (the five phases).
3. Open only the **`workstreams/<area>.md`** you're working on, plus any
   **`reference/`** file it points to. Do **not** read the other workstreams.
4. Follow **`conventions.md`** — especially the sub-agent policy and the
   end-of-session doc-update ritual.

## File map

| File | What it's for |
|---|---|
| `progress.md` | Living status + session log + the current **resume point**. Update every session. |
| `roadmap.md` | The phased plan (P1→P5) and dependencies. |
| `decisions.md` | Decision log (why we chose what) + locked assumptions. |
| `conventions.md` | How we work: sub-agents, doc ritual, code/test/commit rules. |
| `workstreams/backend-data.md` | **P1** — Bun+Hono API, tcgdex→D1 ingest, R2 images, auth, deck API, lobby DO. Contains the tcgdex API reference. |
| `workstreams/deck-builder.md` | **P2** — real cards in the builder, richer filters, editor + decks list. |
| `workstreams/simulator.md` | **P3** — the rules-driven game engine. |
| `workstreams/online.md` | **P4** — run the simulator over the lobby DO for real matches. |
| `workstreams/polish.md` | **P5** — profiles, avatars, lobby names, misc refinement. |
| `reference/ptcg-rules.md` | Condensed Pokémon TCG ruleset — the spec for the simulator (P3). |

**Keep context small.** Delegate research, code-mapping, and multi-file edits to

# Roadmap

Five phases. Each has a detailed workstream doc; this is the map + dependencies.
Live status lives in `progress.md`, not here.

## Phase 1 — Backend & Data Foundation → `workstreams/backend-data.md`
Stand up the Bun + Hono API on Cloudflare. Ingest real tcgdex card data into D1,
mirror images to R2, add accounts + auth (email/password + Discord/Google),
persist decks/folders, and stand up the lobby Durable Object (WebSocket) server.
**Unblocks everything else.**

## Phase 2 — Deck Builder & Decks List (real cards) → `workstreams/deck-builder.md`
Replace the fixture card pool with the live catalog API. Complete the deck
editor (add/remove, counts, format validation, save/load) and the decks list
page (folders, CRUD, persistence). Upgrade filters using the richer tcgdex
fields (set/serie, rarity, HP, illustrator, regulation mark, ability/attack text,
energy cost).
*Depends on: P1 catalog + deck API.*

## Phase 3 — Simulator Engine → `workstreams/simulator.md`
Research the official Pokémon TCG rules (`reference/ptcg-rules.md`) and build the
game engine: a deterministic state machine + a card-effect system driven by the
imported card data + descriptions. Iterative — accuracy improves pass over pass;
unimplemented cards degrade gracefully. The goal is to replicate the real game.
*Depends on: P2 (real, usable decks) + the ruleset.*

## Phase 4 — Online Matches → `workstreams/online.md`
Run the P3 engine authoritatively inside the lobby Durable Object so two players
on different machines can play a real game. Swap the client lobby transport from
BroadcastChannel to WebSocket. Same engine as local play, with tweaks for
authority/hidden info.
*Depends on: P3 engine + P1 lobby DO.*

## Phase 5 — Polish → `workstreams/polish.md`
Now that user + card data exist: player names & profile pictures on the lobby,
profiles, real deck-cover art, and general refinement. Threads through P2–P4 but
tracked separately so it isn't forgotten.
*Depends on: P1 user data.*

1	# Working Conventions
2	
3	## Guidance, not gospel
4	These docs are a **living guide**, not a fixed process. You have context the
5	planning sessions didn't — the actual code, real data, what just broke. Use it:
6	- **Suggest better/different approaches** when you see them. Don't follow a task
7	  list off a cliff because it's written down.
8	- When you deviate: **explain the what + why**, prefer aligning with the user on
9	  anything significant, then **update the affected doc** and log the change in
10	  `decisions.md` (with its rationale). Small in-the-flow improvements don't need
11	  ceremony — just keep the docs honest.
12	- Locked assumptions and D-numbered decisions are **defaults with reasons**, not
13	  laws. Revisit any of them freely; the only hard rule is *don't reverse one
14	  silently* — leave a trail.
15	- Treat file/symbol references in these docs as **point-in-time** — verify against
16	  the current code before relying on them.
17	
18	## Context hygiene (the point of this whole system)
19	- Load **`progress.md` + the one relevant `workstreams/*.md`** (+ its
20	  `reference/`). Don't read unrelated workstreams or sweep the repo.
21	- Prefer facts already written in these docs over re-deriving them.
22	
23	## Sub-agent / workflow policy
24	Delegate to sub-agents to keep the main session's context lean:
25	- **Research** (rules, library docs, API behaviour) → a `general-purpose` agent
26	  that writes a condensed doc into `reference/` and returns only a summary.
27	- **Code mapping** ("how does X work today, what's missing") → an **Explore**
28	  agent (read-only; returns conclusions, not file dumps).
29	- **Implementation** of a self-contained slice → a `general-purpose` agent with
30	  a tight spec; it edits files and returns a summary + what to verify.
31	- **Review** before committing non-trivial work → `/code-review`.
32	- **Big fan-out** (e.g. authoring effect handlers for many cards, or a broad
33	  audit) → a **Workflow** (multi-agent). Note: user-triggered/opt-in — ask first.
34	
35	Rule of thumb: if answering would mean reading many files, delegate it and keep
36	only the conclusion.
37	
38	## Code & quality
39	- TypeScript strict; match the surrounding code's style and comment density.
40	- **Biome** for lint/format; **Vitest** for tests. Run **`bun run check`**
41	  (tsc + biome lint + vitest) before calling work done.
42	- Pure logic gets unit tests (see the many `*.test.ts` in the repo); DOM tests
43	  opt into jsdom per-file (`// @vitest-environment jsdom`).
44	
45	## Git / commits
46	- Branch off `main` for non-trivial work; commit/push only when asked.
47	- Commit trailer per global config: `Co-Authored-By: Claude ...`.
48	
49	## End-of-session ritual (do not skip)
50	1. Update `progress.md`: status table + session-log entry + **new resume point**.
51	2. Record any decision in `decisions.md`.
52	3. Write anything learned into the right workstream/reference doc so the next

# Working Conventions

## Guidance, not gospel
These docs are a **living guide**, not a fixed process. You have context the
planning sessions didn't — the actual code, real data, what just broke. Use it:
- **Suggest better/different approaches** when you see them. Don't follow a task
  list off a cliff because it's written down.
- When you deviate: **explain the what + why**, prefer aligning with the user on
  anything significant, then **update the affected doc** and log the change in
  `decisions.md` (with its rationale). Small in-the-flow improvements don't need
  ceremony — just keep the docs honest.
- Locked assumptions and D-numbered decisions are **defaults with reasons**, not
  laws. Revisit any of them freely; the only hard rule is *don't reverse one
  silently* — leave a trail.
- Treat file/symbol references in these docs as **point-in-time** — verify against
  the current code before relying on them.

## Context hygiene (the point of this whole system)
- Load **`progress.md` + the one relevant `workstreams/*.md`** (+ its
  `reference/`). Don't read unrelated workstreams or sweep the repo.
- Prefer facts already written in these docs over re-deriving them.

## Sub-agent / workflow policy
Delegate to sub-agents to keep the main session's context lean:
- **Research** (rules, library docs, API behaviour) → a `general-purpose` agent
  that writes a condensed doc into `reference/` and returns only a summary.
- **Code mapping** ("how does X work today, what's missing") → an **Explore**
  agent (read-only; returns conclusions, not file dumps).
- **Implementation** of a self-contained slice → a `general-purpose` agent with
  a tight spec; it edits files and returns a summary + what to verify.
- **Review** before committing non-trivial work → `/code-review`.
- **Big fan-out** (e.g. authoring effect handlers for many cards, or a broad
  audit) → a **Workflow** (multi-agent). Note: user-triggered/opt-in — ask first.

Rule of thumb: if answering would mean reading many files, delegate it and keep
only the conclusion.

## Code & quality
- TypeScript strict; match the surrounding code's style and comment density.
- **Biome** for lint/format; **Vitest** for tests. Run **`bun run check`**
  (tsc + biome lint + vitest) before calling work done.
- Pure logic gets unit tests (see the many `*.test.ts` in the repo); DOM tests
  opt into jsdom per-file (`// @vitest-environment jsdom`).

## Git / commits
- Branch off `main` for non-trivial work; commit/push only when asked.
- Commit trailer per global config: `Co-Authored-By: Claude ...`.

## End-of-session ritual (do not skip)
1. Update `progress.md`: status table + session-log entry + **new resume point**.
2. Record any decision in `decisions.md`.
3. Write anything learned into the right workstream/reference doc so the next
   session doesn't rediscover it.

1	# Simulator coverage — the new-op backlog (P3-M5)
2	
3	The engine simulates cards as **data-driven op programs** (registry.ts). A card
4	is playable when its printed effect maps onto the op vocabulary
5	(`effects.ts` EffectOp, plus the continuous/energy/ability shapes in
6	`registry.ts`). M4 built the vocabulary through nine slices; M5 expands **card
7	coverage** across the SV-era pool.
8	
9	## Method — a classify → verify Workflow fan-out (2026-07-19)
10	The 140 un-authored **sv01–sv03** Trainers (61), Special Energies (4) and
11	Pokémon Abilities (75) were classified by a 10-agent fan-out (5 batches ×
12	classify + adversarial verify), each card judged against the current op
13	vocabulary with the deriver doctrine — **exact map or flag** (a wrong-but-plausible
14	program is worse than a flag). Every authorable program was then hand-verified
15	against the local catalog before landing.
16

20	| **authorable now** (landed this pass) | **5** |
21	| needs a new op (backlog below) | 113 |
22	| already authored (M4) | 22 |
23	| **total classified** | 140 |
24	
25	Only ~4% of the un-authored pool is expressible with today's ops — coverage is
26	**op-bound, not authoring-bound**: each new primitive unlocks a whole family, so
27	the backlog below (ranked by cards-unlocked) is the roadmap for the next slices.
28	Authoring is then a few registry rows per card, exactly as D8 intended.

The prompt's `scope` became `{kind:"total",count} \| {kind:"each"}` and the interchangeable collapse now keeps `count` reps per class. STILL BLOCKED after it: the **TYPED** discards (closed by the row below), the multi-sentence riders (**Sandaconda**, **Eiscue ex**, **Weavile**), and **Krookodile**'s flip-until-tails repeat count. |

TWO consumers, one vocabulary (the D40 shape): the **typed self-discard**, DERIVED in both printed notations — the modern "{R}" and the swsh-era spelled-out "Fire" — for **Kilowattrel** (sv01-079), **Arcanine ex ×2** (sv01-032/-224), **Charmeleon** (swsh10.5-009) and **Charizard** (swsh10.5-010) with ZERO registry rows; and **`moveEnergy`'s `benchToActive` route**, authoring **Armarouge ×2** (sv01-041/-203). Rules doc **§9.4**. Lands **Ortega** ×2 (sv03-190/-219, the Miriam shape with both halves across the table) and **Greavard** "Underworld Stroll" (sv01-105) DERIVED from attack text — its Supporter-filtered twin has no second sentence, and its plain second attack (Sharp Fang) is exactly why the per-CARD registry `attack` field could not have carried it. `programPlayable` gained the empty-opponent-hand gate (a PUBLIC count — the Catcher/Hammer class, not Poké Ball's; it reads hand LENGTH and never the filter, since whether a hidden hand holds a match is what the game state does not establish) and is now EXPORTED, so the HUD greys a dead Trainer/Ability row with the predicate that rejects it. |
71	
72	**Long tail (~70 single-card ops)** — e.g. `bounceToHand` (Penny), `moveDamageCounters`
73	(Slowbro), `healBothPlayers` (Picnic Basket), `noRetreatCostAura` (Clefable ex),
74	`removeWeakness` (Florges), `retaliationDamage` (Rocky Helmet), `preventDamageFromExV`
75	(Mimikyu), the Iono/Judge prize-count draws, per-card search filters
76	(`searchFilter:{itemCard,toolCard,evolutionPokemon,…}`), and several bespoke
77	passives/triggers. Full list in the fan-out result. Many collapse into a few
78	parameterized ops (an `attachEnergyFrom` with source/filter params; a
79	`conditionalGate` family; extra `CardFilter` kinds), so the real op count to build
80	is well under 70.
81

100	   Generator / Hydreigon, also 2 attachEnergyFrom cards), the **`conditionalPlay`**
101	   family (5), or the **hand-refresh Supporter family** (Iono/Judge/Marnie).
102	5. ✅ The **hand-refresh Supporter family** — **DONE, row CLOSED** (engine 0.18.0, the
103	   `handRefresh` op: the whole `shuffleHandIntoDeck` row — Youngster / Brassius /

134	   a **`providesEnergy` CardFilter** ("an Energy that PROVIDES {X}" — NOT
135	   `basicEnergy` + type, since a Special Energy providing {L} counts and a

141	   and Krookodile (a flip-until-tails repeat count).

143	   PROVIDES {X}", read by TWO ops — the DERIVED typed self-discard (5 catalog rows,

# Simulator coverage — the new-op backlog (P3-M5)

The engine simulates cards as **data-driven op programs** (registry.ts). A card
is playable when its printed effect maps onto the op vocabulary
(`effects.ts` EffectOp, plus the continuous/energy/ability shapes in
`registry.ts`). M4 built the vocabulary through nine slices; M5 expands **card
coverage** across the SV-era pool.

## Method — a classify → verify Workflow fan-out (2026-07-19)
The 140 un-authored **sv01–sv03** Trainers (61), Special Energies (4) and
Pokémon Abilities (75) were classified by a 10-agent fan-out (5 batches ×
classify + adversarial verify), each card judged against the current op
vocabulary with the deriver doctrine — **exact map or flag** (a wrong-but-plausible
program is worse than a flag). Every authorable program was then hand-verified
against the local catalog before landing.

## Result
| Verdict | Count |
|---|---|
| **authorable now** (landed this pass) | **5** |
| needs a new op (backlog below) | 113 |
| already authored (M4) | 22 |
| **total classified** | 140 |

Only ~4% of the un-authored pool is expressible with today's ops — coverage is
**op-bound, not authoring-bound**: each new primitive unlocks a whole family, so
the backlog below (ranked by cards-unlocked) is the roadmap for the next slices.
Authoring is then a few registry rows per card, exactly as D8 intended.

### Authored this pass (M5 #1)
| Card | id | Program |
|---|---|---|
| Poké Ball | sv01-185 | Item — `coinFlipGate → [searchDeck anyPokemon→hand, shuffleDeck]` |
| Pokémon Catcher | sv01-187 | Item — `coinFlipGate → [gust]` |
| Nemona | sv01-180 | Supporter — `drawCards 3` |
| Copperajah ex (Bronze Body) | sv02-150 | passive `damageReductionAfterWR: 30` |
| Stonjourner (Exoskeleton) | sv01-121 | passive `damageReductionAfterWR: 20` |

(The fan-out mis-placed Poké Ball's `shuffleDeck` *after* the coin gate — it must
be *inside* it, or a tails play reorders the deck; fixed + pinned by a test.)

## New-op backlog — ranked by cards unlocked (sv01–03)
Build these to expand coverage; the count is how many classified cards each
unblocks. High-value ops first.

| New op / capability | Cards | Example cards |
|---|---:|---|
| 🚧 **`attachEnergyFrom`** (attach Energy from hand/discard/deck to a chosen Pokémon) | 11 | **DONE 4/11: Quaquaval, Baxcalibur** (single attach from hand/discard, engine 0.12.0) + **Gardevoir ex** (the `targetType`/`bonusCounters`/`notIfKO` riders, engine 0.13.0) + **Koraidon ex "Dino Cry"** (multi-attach = N ops + `basicOnly` + the `endsTurn` fold, engine 0.14.0). Remaining 7 need MORE ops on top: Forretress ex (deck-search + self-KO), Charizard ex (onEvolve + deck-search-multi), Geeta (deck-search + can't-attack), Electric Generator/Hydreigon (need `lookAtTopN`), Pawmot (deck-search→self, needs the source uid in EffectContext), Wigglytuff (a Special Energy by name) |
| ✅ **`discardPileRetrieval`** (put/shuffle cards from discard → hand/deck) | 6 | **DONE 5/6** — engine 0.15.0 landed the core (the searchDeck mirror + `supporter`/`pokemonOrBasicEnergy` filters): **Energy Retrieval** (2 Basic Energy → hand), **Pal Pad** (2 Supporters → deck), **Super Rod** (3 Pokémon/Basic Energy → deck); engine 0.28.0's §9.2 op→op record landed the two that had to read their own earlier clause: **Superior Energy Retrieval** ×2 (the new `exclude` rider — the cost pays INTO this pile, so without it the payment refunds itself) and **Miriam** ×3 (the new `recordAs` rider + a `recordGate` two ops downstream). Remaining 1: **Pelipper** (an Ability, not a Trainer). |
| ✅ **`lookAtTopN`** (reveal/take a matching card from the top N) | 5 | **DONE 2/5** (engine 0.16.0, the top-of-deck twin of searchDeck: candidates are the top-N matches, then a trailing shuffle): **Great Ball** (top 7 → a Pokémon), **Pokégear 3.0** (top 7 → a Supporter). Remaining 3 need MORE: Electric Generator + Hydreigon attach the found Energy (a from-the-top **attach** variant — the 2 attachEnergyFrom cards this also unblocks), Malamar peeks at the OPPONENT's deck top (a distinct info-only op). |
| ✅ **`moveEnergy`** (move an Energy between your Pokémon) | 5 | **DONE 3/5** (engine 0.17.0, the compound-park own→own op + the `anyEnergy` filter): **Energy Switch** (a Basic Energy, max 1), **Poppy** (up to 2 any Energy, max 2), and — engine 0.24.0, the `route: "benchToActive"` rider + the `providesEnergy` filter — **Armarouge** "Fire Off" (a {R} Energy benched→Active, as often as you like). Remaining 2 need MORE: Mismagius "Magical Flick" (moves the OPPONENT's Energy on evolve — opponent-side + onEvolve trigger), Exp. Share (an on-KO Tool trigger). |
| ✅ **`conditionalPlay`** (a "you can use this only if <board condition>" gate) | 5 | **PRIMITIVE DONE, 1/5 cards** (engine 0.20.0 — the `BoardCondition` vocabulary + its two consumers: the `trainerPlayableIf` PLAY gate and the `conditionGate` branch op): **Fighting Au Lait** (more Prizes left → heal 60). The same vocabulary also lands **Falkner** (Stadium → draw 2 more) and, with `drawUntilHandSize`, **Grusha** — 2 cards from other rows. Remaining 4 each need a SECOND missing piece: **Letter of Encouragement** (a "were any of your Pokémon KO'd during your opponent's LAST turn" state fact — new per-seat history + flow wiring), ~~**Dendra**~~ (**DONE**, engine 0.27.0 — the gate turned out to be §7.5's hand COST, not a `BoardCondition`: `payFromHand` `to: "deckBottom"` + `drawUntilHandSize`), **Luxray** (an in-hand Ability surface — abilities are in-play only today), **Lunatone** (Stadium-effect prevention). Next reader of the same vocabulary: **Defiance Band** (a conditional PASSIVE — the third consumer). |
| ✅ **`discardOpponentEnergy`** (discard an Energy from an opponent's Pokémon) | 4 | **DONE 3/4** (engine 0.21.0 — the `discardEnergy` op + the `specialEnergy` filter; ONE op whose `from` names both the eligible Pokémon and how many are hit, all three arms landing with a real card): **Crushing Hammer** (`opponentChosen`, behind a coin flip), **Giacomo** (`opponentEach` — one Special Energy off EVERY one of their Pokémon that has one), **Mawile** (`opponentActive`, an onPlayToBench trigger). Remaining 1: **Klawf ex**, which needs `onDamagedByAttack` (the row below), not more of this op. |
| ✅ **attack effect programs that can PARK** (a mid-attack `effect:choose`) | ~13 | **DONE — the mechanism (engine 0.22.0), plus 12 catalog rows of its first family.** A new `attackEpilogue` PendingStage carries the §8.1 KO sweep + the §5.3 turn end; `attack.ts` seeds it BEFORE the effect program runs and folds through `settleProgram`'s `resumeTail`, so a parked prompt and the ops behind it survive. Landed with it: `discardEnergy` gained a **`yourActive`** arm and a **`count: "all"`** rider, both DERIVED from the printed sentence (no registry rows) — "Discard an Energy from this Pokémon." covers **Houndoom ×2 (sv01-034, sv03-133), Charcadet, Staraptor, Paldean Tauros, Dedenne ex ×2, Bombirdier**; "Discard all Energy from this Pokémon." covers **Pawmot ×2, Raichu ×2**. |
| ✅ **the discardEnergy ATTACK arms** — the opponent-side twins + the exact-N count | 11 | **DONE (engine 0.23.0), again with ZERO registry rows — two deriver sentences and one widened field.** The **twins** ("Discard an Energy from your opponent's Active Pokémon.", bare and behind a flip) run the EXISTING `opponentActive` arm with an `anyEnergy` filter: **Pincurchin** (sv02-072), **Gumshoos** (sv03-177), **Dragonite V ×2** (swsh10.5-049/-076); **Dedenne** (sv01-094), **Maschiff** (sv01-136), **Tympole** (sv03-050), **Yveltal** (sv06.5-035). The **exact-N** self-discard widens `count` from `"all"` to any number: **Corviknight** (sv02-148), **Slither Wing** (sv06.5-026), **Koraidon** (sv01-124). The prompt's `scope` became `{kind:"total",count} \| {kind:"each"}` and the interchangeable collapse now keeps `count` reps per class. STILL BLOCKED after it: the **TYPED** discards (closed by the row below), the multi-sentence riders (**Sandaconda**, **Eiscue ex**, **Weavile**), and **Krookodile**'s flip-until-tails repeat count. |
| ✅ **the `providesEnergy` CardFilter** — "an Energy that PROVIDES {X}" | 7 | **DONE (engine 0.24.0) — the last missing piece of the energy-discard family, and the first filter a CARD alone cannot answer.** "{L} Energy" is not "a Basic Lightning card": a Special providing {L} IS one, a wildcard (Luminous) is one of EVERY type, and provision is a while-ATTACHED property that Luminous's own text makes depend on the holder's other attachments — so the predicate reads what an Energy gives ON ITS HOST, through the very code §8.2's cost matcher reads (`unitsProvidedBy`). `matchesFilter`, the deck/hand/discard scanner, answers FALSE for it (a card in a pile is attached to nothing), so authoring it into a pile-scanning op is a loud no-op rather than a wrong card. TWO consumers, one vocabulary (the D40 shape): the **typed self-discard**, DERIVED in both printed notations — the modern "{R}" and the swsh-era spelled-out "Fire" — for **Kilowattrel** (sv01-079), **Arcanine ex ×2** (sv01-032/-224), **Charmeleon** (swsh10.5-009) and **Charizard** (swsh10.5-010) with ZERO registry rows; and **`moveEnergy`'s `benchToActive` route**, authoring **Armarouge ×2** (sv01-041/-203). STILL BLOCKED, and now every one of them for sentence STRUCTURE rather than for any missing filter: **Pawmot ex** (a typed discard plus "220 damage to 1 of your opponent's Pokémon" — `damageChosen` exists but targets the Bench, not any Pokémon), **Bellibolt ex** ("you may … to make it Paralyzed" — an optional discard BUYING an effect), **Chien-Pao ex** / **Mewtwo VSTAR** (a variable count with damage scaling off it), **Sandaconda** / **Eiscue ex** / **Weavile** (rider clauses) and **Krookodile** (a repeat count). |
| ✅ **`discardFromHandCost`** → **`payFromHand`** (pay N cards out of hand to play) | 4 | **DONE 3/4, and the row's real size was bigger than this count** (engine 0.26.0 — the printed COST that PARKS, so it is an OP at the head of its program rather than a field paid before it). Two printed wordings, ONE mechanism, and the wording tracks where the paying card sits: TRAINERS say "only if you discard 2 **other** cards" because the card is in the hand it pays from — **Ultra Ball** (sv01-196), **Earthen Vessel** (sv06.5-096, "another card"); ABILITIES never say "other" because the card is on the board — **Revavroom** (sv01-142, "an Energy card" → draw to 6, the ORDER witness), **Tinkaton** (sv02-105, "a card" → draw 3, the unfiltered general case). The same sentence is printed on **Meowscarada ex** and **Radiant Blastoise** (swsh10.5-018), so the old `AbilityProgram.cost` field — which could only express the FUNGIBLE case — was REMOVED and Meowscarada migrated onto the op: 9 catalog rows in all. `chooseCards` gained a required `min` (the first MANDATORY card park; every "up to" consumer declares 0). **Row CLOSED at engine 0.28.0**: **Superior Energy Retrieval** (sv02-189/-277) landed with the §9.2 record, its "(You can't choose a card you discarded with the effect of this card.)" becoming `discardPileRetrieval.exclude` reading the uids `payFromHand` filed. |
| **`onDamagedByAttack`** (a trigger firing when damaged by an attack, even if KO'd) | 4 | Cacnea, Cacturne, Armarouge, Klawf ex |
| ✅ **`shuffleHandIntoDeck` (+ draw)** — the Iono/Judge hand-refresh family | 3 | **DONE — row CLOSED, +Judge +Iono** (the `handRefresh` op: engine 0.18.0 fully-automatic, reaches the OPPONENT): **Youngster** (draw 5), **Brassius** (draw hand+1), **Katy** (draw 8 + turn ends), **Judge** (both shuffle + draw 4), and **Iono** (engine 0.19.0 — the `toBottom` placement so the deck's ORDER survives, a `prizeCount` draw, and the `onlyIfAnyMoved` cross-seat draw gate). No Marnie exists in the sv01–03 catalog. The other bottom-of-deck cards: **Dendra** (**DONE** engine 0.27.0 — a CHOSEN card, so it is `payFromHand` `to: "deckBottom"`, not this op) and **Skwovet** ×2 "Nest Stash" (**DONE** engine 0.27.0 — this op exactly, `toBottom` + `onlyIfAnyMoved` + a fixed draw of 1, on the ABILITY path; zero new code). Still open: none — **Ortega** landed in engine 0.32.0 (`bottomFromOpponentHand`, the row below). |
| **`stadiumActivatedAbility`** (a "once during each player's turn" Stadium) | 3 | Artazon, Mesagoza, Town Store |
| **`damageAttacker`** (put counters on the attacking Pokémon) | 3 | Cacnea, Cacturne, Stunfisk |
| **`disableAbilities`** (a continuous Ability-lock aura) | 3 | Klefki, Spiritomb, Ting-Lu ex |
| ✅ `drawUntilHandSize` | 2 | **DONE — row CLOSED 2/2.** (engine 0.20.0 — draws to a floor, never TRIMS a bigger hand; no event at a count ≤ 0): **Grusha** (to 5, or to 7 with no Energy on your board — the `conditionGate` `otherwise` arm), and — engine 0.27.0 — **Dendra** (draw to 5, counting the card just paid to the bottom of the deck: the payment is the program's FIRST op, so a hand of 4 draws three). |
| ✅ `endTurn` (a play that ends your turn) | 2 | **DONE**: Koraidon ex (the `AbilityProgram.endsTurn` fold, engine 0.14.0) + Katy (the same fold on the Trainer path via `trainerEndsTurn`, engine 0.18.0). |
| `conditionalDamageBonus` (Tool: +N under a condition) | 2 | Choice Belt, Defiance Band |
| `statusImmunity` / `preventDamageFromType` / `coinFlipDamagePrevention` / `drawUntil` / `canEvolveEarly` | 2 each | Dachsbun, Bellibolt, Jumpluff/Skiploom, Togekiss, Scatterbug/Spewpa |
| ✅ **the hand cost paid UNDER THE DECK** (`payFromHand`'s `to: "deckBottom"`) | 5 | **DONE — the same op one field wider, plus one card that needed no op at all** (engine 0.27.0). **Dendra** ×3 (sv02-179/-250/-266): "Put a card from your hand on the bottom of your deck. If you do, draw cards until you have 5 cards in your hand. (If you have no other cards in your hand, you can't use this card.)" — nothing is discarded and the word "cost" never appears, but it is the same mandatory exact pick, the same conditional benefit ("if you do") and the same printed play gate, stated as its contrapositive with the same word "other". So `discardFromHandCost` became **`payFromHand`** with a required `to: "discard" \| "deckBottom"`, and `handCostUnmet` gates the card with no new code. **Skwovet** ×2 (sv01-151/-222) "Nest Stash" reaches the same destination with the WHOLE hand — `handRefresh` + Iono's `toBottom` + `onlyIfAnyMoved`, ZERO new ops, and the first `handRefresh` on the Ability path. No longer blocked: **Ortega** reaches the same destination on the OPPONENT's side and got its own op (engine 0.32.0, the row below) — the hand it reads is REVEALED by the effect, which is what `payFromHand` could never say. |
| ✅ **"choose N" is EXACT** (`choosePokemonMulti`'s `min`/`max` + `declinable`) | — | **DONE (engine 0.27.0) — a rules FIX, not a coverage row.** The printed number in a *choose* clause is a floor as well as a ceiling (rules doc **§9.1**), so Meowscarada ex / Radiant Blastoise can no longer pay their irreversible hand cost and then place nothing, and Hawlucha's "**you may** choose 2" is all-or-nothing (2 or none, never 1 of 2 — its trigger auto-fires, so the pick is the only place its "may" can live). The next consumer that will need the OTHER end of the range is **Janine's Secret Art** ("choose **up to** 2 of your {D} Pokémon"). |
| ✅ **§9.2 — a clause that reads what an earlier clause DID** (the op→op record) | 5 | **DONE (engine 0.28.0) — the engine's first op→op data flow, and the last mechanism the `payFromHand` and `discardPileRetrieval` rows were waiting on.** Some printed clauses cannot be answered from the board, because the board after an effect looks the same whether a card got there by that effect or was already sitting there. So an op files the uids it MOVED under a named `EffectSlot` (`recordAs`), and a later op reads them. TWO readers, one record (the D40 shape): the **gate** — a new `recordGate {slot, then, otherwise?}`, spliced into the work queue like the other two gates — landing **Miriam** ×3 (sv01-179/-238/-251, "If you shuffled any cards into your deck **in this way**, draw 3 cards") and finally letting **Dendra** state its own printed "**If you do**"; and the **exclusion** — `discardPileRetrieval.exclude` — landing **Superior Energy Retrieval** ×2 (sv02-189/-277), whose cost pays INTO the very pile its next clause reads, so without it a player discards 2 Basic Energy and takes the same two straight back. The record is keyed by UID, not by card id (an identical print already in the pile stays choosable), and by SLOT, not by position: Miriam prints a deck shuffle BETWEEN the retrieval and the sentence about it, so "the previous op" was never a workable reading of "in this way" — the same shape **Janine's Secret Art** prints. It rides `EffectContinuation.record` (an accumulator, sibling to `rest`) rather than `EffectContext` (a constant), and is absent when empty, so every program predating §9.2 parks into a byte-identical phase. Both cards this row left open have since landed: **Janine's Secret Art** (engine 0.29.0 — the per-target deck search, whose own gate is the `contains` narrowing) and **Ortega** (engine 0.32.0 — the gate over an opponent-side pick, the row two below). |
| ✅ **the reveal-and-bottom family + the OPPONENT's own decision** (`bottomFromOpponentHand` + `opponentMayDraw`) | 3 | **DONE (engine 0.32.0) — the last row the §9.2 and `payFromHand` rows both left open, and it needed a mechanism neither of them did.** Two ops. `bottomFromOpponentHand` reveals the opponent's whole hand (a new PUBLIC `HAND_REVEALED` naming every uid — that is what the printed word means at a table, and it is the one hand event in the file that is not count-only), the controller picks one card, and it goes under the OPPONENT's deck (`CARD_TO_BOTTOM_OF_DECK`, named, with an `actor`: unlike Dendra's payment this move happened face up at BOTH ends, so which card sits on the bottom is real public information). The offer collapses to one representative per interchangeable class — sound here precisely where it is not in `payFromHand`, whose collapse over a still-hidden hand leaks its duplicate structure. `opponentMayDraw` is the engine's **first decision answered by the NON-controller**: the park carries a `decider`, the phase a `answerer` beside its controller `seat` (absent when they agree, so every older park serializes byte-identically), and `resolveEffect` admits only that seat — the controller cannot consent for them. Rules doc **§9.4**. Lands **Ortega** ×2 (sv03-190/-219, the Miriam shape with both halves across the table) and **Greavard** "Underworld Stroll" (sv01-105) DERIVED from attack text — its Supporter-filtered twin has no second sentence, and its plain second attack (Sharp Fang) is exactly why the per-CARD registry `attack` field could not have carried it. `programPlayable` gained the empty-opponent-hand gate (a PUBLIC count — the Catcher/Hammer class, not Poké Ball's; it reads hand LENGTH and never the filter, since whether a hidden hand holds a match is what the game state does not establish) and is now EXPORTED, so the HUD greys a dead Trainer/Ability row with the predicate that rejects it. |

**Long tail (~70 single-card ops)** — e.g. `bounceToHand` (Penny), `moveDamageCounters`
(Slowbro), `healBothPlayers` (Picnic Basket), `noRetreatCostAura` (Clefable ex),
`removeWeakness` (Florges), `retaliationDamage` (Rocky Helmet), `preventDamageFromExV`

One-armed is the common shape (Falkner); `otherwise` exists for the printed "…**instead**", a genuine if/ELSE (Grusha). Falkner's PAIR of draw rows and Grusha's zero-row case); the export's "a P4 client may evaluate one locally" claim was **self-defeating** (see below); and the HUD's opponent-`prizes` read. **P4 item recorded, not fixed:** `conditionHolds` takes a `GameState`, so only a raw-state host can run it — the projection does NOT carry `stadium.owner` and redacts the prize arrays. Three printed wordings, one mechanism: Miriam's "if you shuffled any cards into your deck **in this way**", Dendra's "**if you do**", and Superior Energy Retrieval's "(You can't choose a card you discarded with **the effect of this card**.)". **THE SHAPE:** an op files the uids it ACTUALLY moved under a named **`EffectSlot`** (`recordAs`), and later ops read them — **TWO readers, one record** (the D40 two-consumers shape): a new **`recordGate {slot, then, otherwise?}`**, the third and last gate, spliced into runProgram's work queue exactly like `coinFlipGate`/`conditionGate` so an op inside a branch can still park; and **`discardPileRetrieval.exclude`**, which drops them from a candidate set. SER is what makes the second one load-bearing rather than cosmetic — its cost pays INTO the very discard pile its next clause reads, so without the exclusion a player discards 2 Basic Energy and takes the same two straight back, the cost refunds itself, and the parenthetical the printer added to stop exactly that means nothing. **THE RECORD RIDES `EffectContinuation`, NOT `EffectContext`** — a deliberate deviation from what the backlog named for three slices. The context is WHO the program runs for: one seat, constant for the whole program, read by ~30 helpers that would then hold a value going stale under them mid-run. This is the opposite, an accumulator changing at nearly every op, so its sibling is **`rest`** ("the ops still to run"), not `seat`; it is threaded like `events` and is ABSENT when empty, so every program predating §9.2 parks into a byte-identical phase. **KEYED BY SLOT, NOT BY POSITION.** "Read the previous op's result" is the obvious cheaper design and it is wrong: Janine's Secret Art prints a whole sentence between the action and the clause about it ("Then, shuffle your deck. If you attached Energy … in this way, …"), and Miriam — whose two sentences ARE adjacent on the card — stops being adjacent under the natural decomposition of "shuffle N into your deck" (a move plus a trailing `shuffleDeck`, the Pal Pad pattern). A closed 2-member union makes a mistyped slot a COMPILE error, which matters because an unrecorded slot reads as "nothing moved" — indistinguishable from a real empty answer, so a typo would silently cost Miriam its draw. Keyed by **uid**, not card id: a second copy of the identical print already in the pile stays choosable, which is the printed sentence read literally. 222	  // printed base; MULTIPLY ("×", no "more") makes `per × count` the WHOLE damage,
223	  // the printed base dropped. Their regexes are mutually exclusive, so at most one
224	  // fires — read multiply only when additive did not, making that explicit. A card
225	  // carries at most one scaling clause OR a program: the whole-sentence anchor
226	  // means a scaling sentence never also derives an op.
227	  const damageBonus = effect === null || effect === "" ? null : deriveAttackDamageBonus(effect);

229	    damageBonus !== null || effect === null || effect === ""

233	  const scaled = scaling === null ? 0 : scaledAttackDamage(active, scaling, next, defenderSeat);

235	  // `scaled`), so it is dropped from the pipeline — the additive family keeps its
236	  // printed base. count 0 → scaled 0 → no damage (the base does not leak through).
237	  const scaledBase = damageMultiplier !== null ? 0 : base;
238	  // The "+"/"×" modifier is SIMULATED iff a scaling reader consumed it; the
239	  // effect text is simulated iff a program ran it OR a scaling reader did. Only
240	  // the genuinely-unsimulated remainder is flagged loudly (simulator.md coverage).
241	  const effectSimulated = program !== null || scaling !== null;
242	  const modifierSimulated = scaling !== null;
243	  if (
244	    (modifier !== null && !modifierSimulated) ||
245	    (effect !== null && effect !== "" && !effectSimulated)
246	  ) {
247	    events.push({
248	      type: "ATTACK_EFFECT_SKIPPED",
249	      seat: action.seat,
250	      attack: declared.name,
251	      // Authored/derived/scaled text IS simulated — only an unsimulated one is skipped.
252	      effect: effectSimulated ? null : effect,
253	      damageModifier: modifierSimulated ? null : modifier,
254	    });
255	  }
256	
257	  let defended = defender;
258	  if (scaledBase + scaled > 0) {
259	    // §8.5 damage pipeline, in printed order: base + the attack's own printed
260	    // scaling clause (`scaled` — Paldean Tauros "Raging Horns", counted at
261	    // declaration) + the attacker's continuous pre-W/R bonus (Vitality Band) →
262	    // Weakness (modern ×2, the old-era +20 prints add) → Resistance (−30) → the
263	    // defender's continuous damage reduction (Bouffalant "Bouffer" / a defending
264	    // Tool, §15.B), floored at 0. Weakness/Resistance apply to the Defending
265	    // Pokémon only, and both continuous reads aggregate printed passives WITH
266	    // attached Tools (continuous.ts). `scaled` is the attack's own damage (added
267	    // alongside the continuous bonus at the same pre-W/R step), so this branch
268	    // fires whenever the (multiply-adjusted) base OR the scaling clause does
269	    // damage. `scaledBase` is `base` except for a multiply clause, whose printed
270	    // "N×" base is the per-unit already inside `scaled` — so it is 0 here.
271	    const bonus = passivesOf(next, active).damageBonusBeforeWR;
272	    const weakness = weaknessOf(attacker, defenderCard);
273	    const resistance = resistanceOf(attacker, defenderCard);
274	    const afterWR = Math.max(
275	      0,
276	      applyDamageModifier(applyDamageModifier(scaledBase + scaled + bonus, weakness), resistance),
277	    );
278	    const reduction = passivesOf(next, defender).damageReductionAfterWR;
279	    const dealt = Math.max(0, afterWR - reduction);
280	    defended = { ...defender, damage: defender.damage + dealt };
281	    next = withSide(next, defenderSeat, { ...next.players[defenderSeat], active: defended });
282	    events.push({
283	      type: "DAMAGE_DEALT",
284	      seat: defenderSeat,
285	      uid: defenderUid,
286	      base: scaledBase,
287	      // Present only when the printed scaling clause actually added HP.
288	      scaled: scaled > 0 ? scaled : undefined,
289	      // Present only when a continuous effect actually moved the total.
290	      bonus: bonus > 0 ? bonus : undefined,
291	      weakness,
292	      resistance,
293	      reduction: reduction > 0 ? reduction : undefined,
294	      dealt,
295	      damage: defended.damage,
296	    });
297	  }

299	  // §8 step 4 — the effect program runs AFTER the damage, in printed order: a
300	  // defender-targeted status lands even when the damage above is lethal (the
301	  // condition vanishes with the stack at the KO below).
302	  //
303	  // The program may PARK on a decision ("Discard an Energy from this Pokémon"
304	  // with two different Energy attached), and an attack that parks must still
305	  // finish afterwards — so the epilogue is QUEUED as a stage before the program
306	  // runs, and the fold goes through settleProgram with `resumeTail`. A DONE
307	  // program drains straight into it (identical to the pre-slice inline call, one
308	  // hop later); a parked one leaves it sitting in `pending` until resolveEffect
309	  // finishes the program and drains it then. APPENDED rather than assigned: the
310	  // queue is empty here (turn:action never carries a tail — the three writers of
311	  // that phase all leave it empty), so this is the same thing, but a stage that
312	  // somehow WAS queued would run after the attack instead of vanishing.
313	  if (program !== null) {
314	    const epilogue: PendingStage = {
315	      kind: "attackEpilogue",
316	      seat: action.seat,
317	    };
318	    return settleProgram(
319	      runProgram(
320	        { ...next, pending: [...next.pending, epilogue] },
321	        program,
322	        // The attacker is "this Pokémon" (§8) — by uid rather than "the Active",
323	        // which stays truthful if the program itself moves it off the spot.
324	        { seat: action.seat, sourceUid: attackerUid },
325	        events,
326	      ),
327	      action.seat,
328	      events,
329	      { resumeTail: true },

333	  // §8.1 Knock Out sweep on both boards, then the §5.3 turn end — the shared
334	  // epilogue with the confusion-tails exit above. With no effect program there is
335	  // no recoil, so only the defender's board can be lethal, but the sweep stays
336	  // total (finishAttack owns the order + the §14 tie).
337	  return finishAttack(next, events, action.seat);

# Defiance Band implementation — findings report

## 1. Defiance Band & Choice Belt catalog data

The printed rules text is **not** in any JSON/TS fixture — the `packages/schema/.../set-full-sv01.json` fixture is only a set *index* (id/name/image/localId). The actual effect text lives in the **D1/SQLite catalog**, table `cards`, column `effect` (`apps/api/src/db/catalog.ts:92` — `effect: text("effect")`, commented "Trainer/Energy rules text"). Category/subtype live in `cards.category` (`catalog.ts:71`) and `cards.trainer_type` (`catalog.ts:89`).

Queried read-only from `apps/api/.wrangler/state/v3/d1/miniflare-D1DatabaseObject/8437….sqlite`:

- **Defiance Band** — id **`sv01-169`**, category `Trainer`, trainer_type `Tool`. Exact effect string:
  > "If you have more Prize cards remaining than your opponent, the attacks of the Pokémon this card is attached to do 30 more damage to your opponent's Active Pokémon (before applying Weakness and Resistance)."
- **Choice Belt** — id **`sv02-176`**, category `Trainer`, trainer_type `Tool`. Exact effect string:
  > "The attacks of the Pokémon this card is attached to do 30 more damage to your opponent's Active Pokémon V (before applying Weakness and Resistance)."
  (Note the "…Active Pokémon **V**" — this is the Pokémon-V-only wording, an unconditional +30 gated on the *target* being a V, not a board condition.)

**Authoring status:** Neither is authored in the engine registry. `grep` for `sv01-169`/`Defiance` and `Choice Belt`/`CHOICE` in `packages/engine/src/registry.ts` returns nothing (the only "choice" hits are unrelated prose). Both are catalog-only today. The backlog row confirms both are pending: `docs/reference/coverage-backlog.md:65` — `| conditionalDamageBonus (Tool: +N under a condition) | 2 | Choice Belt, Defiance Band |`, and Defiance Band is called out as "the third consumer" of the `BoardCondition` vocabulary at `coverage-backlog.md:52` and `:114`.

## 2. The `damageReductionAfterWR` passive (closest analog)

(a) **Shape/type defined** — `packages/engine/src/registry.ts:91-107`, interface `PassiveEffects`:
```ts
export interface PassiveEffects {
  /** …applied AFTER Weakness and Resistance (Bouffalant "Bouffer", §8.5/§15.B). */
  damageReductionAfterWR?: number;
  /** …applied BEFORE Weakness and Resistance (Vitality Band). */
  damageBonusBeforeWR?: number;
  /** Max-HP added while the holder's TOP card is a Basic (Bravery Charm). */
  basicHpBonus?: number;
}
```
`PassiveEffects` is attached to a card via `CardProgram.passive` (`registry.ts:178`).

(b) **Registry rows** — the two card programs at `registry.ts:679` and `:683`:
```ts
const COPPERAJAH_EX: CardProgram = { passive: { damageReductionAfterWR: 30 } };  // :679
const STONJOURNER:  CardProgram = { passive: { damageReductionAfterWR: 20 } };  // :683
```
Wired into the id→program map at `registry.ts:1613-1614`:
```ts
"sv02-150": COPPERAJAH_EX, // Bronze Body (−30 after W/R)
"sv01-121": STONJOURNER,   // Exoskeleton (−20 after W/R)
```
(A third, `BOUFFALANT` `damageReductionAfterWR: 20` at `:262`, row `"sv03-174"` at `:1567`, is the printed-Ability analog.)

(c) **Applied in damage calc** — aggregated in `continuous.ts:39-62` `passivesOf(state, pokemon)` (sums every source: the top card's `passive` plus every attached Tool's `passive`), then read at the DEFENDER at:
- `attack.ts:278-279` (main hit): `const reduction = passivesOf(next, defender).damageReductionAfterWR; const dealt = Math.max(0, afterWR - reduction);`
- `interpreter.ts:1210-1211` (spread/bench), `:1278-1279` (Covetous Ivy bench attack damage), `:1322-1323` (snipeActive on the opponent's Active).

(d) **Unit tests** — `packages/engine/src/coverage.test.ts:141-159`:
```ts
it("Copperajah ex's Bronze Body reduces attack damage by 30 (after W/R)", () => {
  … state = setActiveFromDeck(state, "p2", "sv02-150");
  expect(find(events, "DAMAGE_DEALT")).toMatchObject({ base: 30, reduction: 30, dealt: 0 });
  expect(after.players.p2.active?.damage).toBe(0); }); // 30 − 30 floored
```
Stonjourner mirror at `:151-159` asserts `{ base: 30, reduction: 20, dealt: 10 }`. Also `src/features/game/demoDecks.test.ts:64` asserts `programFor("sv03-174")?.passive?.damageReductionAfterWR === 20`.

## 3. The full attack-damage pipeline

End-to-end computation lives in **`packages/engine/src/attack.ts`, function `attack(state, action)` (`attack.ts:110`)**. Base damage is parsed at `attack.ts:210` (`parseAttackDamage(declared.damage)` → `{ base, modifier }`, defined `cards.ts:115`). The scaling clause (`scaled`) is computed at `:233`. The core §8.5 arithmetic is `attack.ts:271-279`:
```ts
const bonus     = passivesOf(next, active).damageBonusBeforeWR;         // :271 additive, pre-W/R
const weakness  = weaknessOf(attacker, defenderCard);                  // :272
const resistance= resistanceOf(attacker, defenderCard);                // :273
const afterWR = Math.max(0,
  applyDamageModifier(applyDamageModifier(scaledBase + scaled + bonus, weakness), resistance)); // :274-277
const reduction = passivesOf(next, defender).damageReductionAfterWR;    // :278 subtractive, post-W/R
const dealt     = Math.max(0, afterWR - reduction);                     // :279 floor at 0
```
**Exact order:** `base` (`scaledBase`) → `+ scaled` (attack's own printed scaling clause) → `+ bonus` (continuous pre-W/R additive) → Weakness (`applyDamageModifier` multiply×2, `cards.ts:161/176`) → Resistance (subtract 30, `cards.ts:167/180`) → `− reduction` (post-W/R) → `Math.max(0, …)`. W/R apply to the Active/Defender only.

**The hook point for Defiance Band's "+30 before W/R" is the `bonus` term at `attack.ts:271`** (inside the `scaledBase + scaled + bonus` sum). 

**A pre-W/R additive mechanism already exists and is exactly the right one: `damageBonusBeforeWR` (Vitality Band).** It is UNCONDITIONAL today. Defiance Band is the *conditional* variant of the same field. The same `bonus` read is mirrored in `interpreter.ts:1315` for `snipeActive` (a snipe landing on the opponent's Active). Note `scaledBase + scaled + bonus` is only entered when `scaledBase + scaled > 0` (`attack.ts:258`) — i.e. a 0-damage attack gets no bonus, matching the card wording.

## 4. Tool cards & passives in the registry

Tools are represented as ordinary catalog cards (`category: "Trainer"`, `trainer_type: "Tool"`) whose behaviour is a `CardProgram` with a **`passive: PassiveEffects`** entry. The passive registry is keyed by card id — `packages/engine/src/registry.ts`, the big id→`CardProgram` map (rows ~`1560-1690`), read through **`programFor(id)`** (imported in `continuous.ts:12`). A Tool with a `passive` entry is attachable; one without is "not simulated" (`registry.ts:176-178` comment).

Enumeration of "Tools attached to the attacking Pokémon" happens in **`continuous.ts:39-62` `passivesOf`**:
```ts
const sources = [
  top === undefined ? undefined : programFor(top.id)?.passive,   // the holder's own printed passive
  ...pokemon.tools.map((uid) => {                                 // every attached Tool
    const id = state.cardIdByUid[uid];
    return id === undefined ? undefined : programFor(id)?.passive;
  }),
];
… for (const passive of sources) { … damageBonusBeforeWR += passive.damageBonusBeforeWR ?? 0; … }
```
So a Pokémon's attached Tool uids are `InPlayPokemon.tools` (array of uids), resolved to card ids via `state.cardIdByUid[uid]`, then to a program via `programFor(id).passive`. Existing per-Tool passives: `VITALITY_BAND` (`registry.ts:277`, `damageBonusBeforeWR: 10`, row `"sv01-197"` at `:1574`) and `BRAVERY_CHARM` (`:281`, `basicHpBonus: 50`, row `"sv02-173"` at `:1576`).

**Key architectural note for the conditional shape:** `passivesOf(state, pokemon)` takes only `state` + the Pokémon — it has **no seat and no condition context**, and it aggregates all sources into flat sums. A conditional bonus therefore cannot be expressed by summing a plain number inside `passivesOf` unless you either (a) thread the owning `Seat` into `passivesOf` so it can call `conditionHolds`, or (b) add a new field carrying the `BoardCondition` and evaluate it at the two read sites that DO know the attacker's seat (`attack.ts:271` has `action.seat`; `interpreter.ts:1315` has `ctx.seat`). See Q5 for seat availability.

## 5. The `BoardCondition` vocabulary

**Union definition** — `packages/engine/src/effects.ts:156-168`:
```ts
export type BoardCondition =
  | { kind: "morePrizesThanOpponent" }   // :160  (comment :157-159 names Defiance Band explicitly)
  | { kind: "yourStadiumInPlay" }        // :164
  | { kind: "noEnergyOnYourPokemon" };   // :168
```
The comment at `effects.ts:157-159` already earmarks this member for Defiance Band. `BoardCondition` is imported into `interpreter.ts:18`.

**`conditionHolds`** — `interpreter.ts:1011-1023` (signature takes `GameState`, `Seat`, `BoardCondition`):
```ts
export function conditionHolds(state: GameState, seat: Seat, cond: BoardCondition): boolean {
  switch (cond.kind) {
    case "morePrizesThanOpponent":
      return state.players[seat].prizes.length > state.players[otherSeat(seat)].prizes.length; // :1014
    …
```

**`conditionNote`** (the printed-text describer) — also in `interpreter.ts`, `:1027-1036`:
```ts
export function conditionNote(cond: BoardCondition): string {
  switch (cond.kind) {
    case "morePrizesThanOpponent":
      return "you have more Prize cards remaining than your opponent"; // :1030
    …
```

**Seat access from the damage calc:** Yes. `attack(state, action)` has the full `GameState` (`next`) and both seats — `action.seat` is the attacker, `defenderSeat = otherSeat(action.seat)` (`attack.ts:160`). So `conditionHolds(next, action.seat, { kind: "morePrizesThanOpponent" })` evaluates the condition for the *attacking* seat directly at the `attack.ts:271` hook. The `snipeActive` mirror at `interpreter.ts:1305-1315` has `ctx.seat` (the attacker) and `state`, so it can call `conditionHolds(state, ctx.seat, …)` the same way. `passivesOf` itself does **not** receive a seat today (`continuous.ts:39`), so the condition must be evaluated at those call sites (or a seat threaded in).

## 6. Engine version + changelog

Confirmed: **`packages/engine/src/index.ts:247` — `export const engineVersion = "0.41.0";`**. There is **no separate CHANGELOG file** (`find -iname CHANGELOG` → none). The version history is a JSDoc comment block immediately above the constant (`index.ts` ~`:150-246`), one dated paragraph per minor bump (…`0.39.0`, `0.40.0`, `0.41.0` at `:233-246`). Bump this block + the constant per slice. Also cross-check the backlog framing in `docs/reference/coverage-backlog.md` (rows `:52`, `:65`, `:108-115`) and `docs/progress.md`.

## 7. Test conventions for passives

Two representative files to mirror:
- **`packages/engine/src/stadiumTool.test.ts:279-313`** — `describe("Vitality Band — +10 damage before Weakness/Resistance")`. This is the **direct analog** for Defiance Band (a Tool with a pre-W/R additive). It builds a board with `p1Turn2(6)`, sets actives via `setActiveFromDeck(state, "p1", "fix-attacker")` / `"fix-wall"` / `"fix-weak"`, pays cost with `attachFromDeck(…, "fix-energy", 1)`, draws the Tool with `handFromDeck(state,"p1","sv01-197",1)` + `handUid`, attaches via `applyAction(…, { type:"attachTool", seat:"p1", uid, target:{spot:"active"} })`, attacks with `mustApply(state, { type:"attack", seat:"p1", index:0 })`, then asserts on the `DAMAGE_DEALT` event via `find(events,"DAMAGE_DEALT")`: `expect(dealt?.base).toBe(30); expect(dealt?.bonus).toBe(10); expect(dealt?.dealt).toBe(40)`. The `:298-312` case pins the **before-W/R** ordering: `(30+10)×2 = 80` against `fix-weak` (a wrong after-W/R impl would give 70).
- **`packages/engine/src/coverage.test.ts:141-159`** — the reduction analog, using `covBoard(n)` + the `bite` attack action + `find(events,"DAMAGE_DEALT")` `.toMatchObject({ base, reduction, dealt })` + `after.players.p2.active?.damage`.

**Fixtures/helpers** are all in `packages/engine/src/testFixtures.ts`: board builders `p1Turn2` / `covBoard(n)` (n = a per-suite deck-count key, see the count tables ~`:1616-2252`); `setActiveFromDeck` (`:2276`), `attachFromDeck` (`:2486`), `handFromDeck` (`:2550`), `handUid` (`:2404`), `handUids` (`:2412`), `must` (`:2351`), `mustApply` (`:2357`). Battler fixtures: `fix-attacker` (`:145`, its "Bite" costs `[C]`, base 30), `fix-wall` (120 HP, `:211`), `fix-weak` (60 HP, ×2 Fire, `:213`). Damage is asserted off the emitted `DAMAGE_DEALT` GameEvent (fields `base/scaled/bonus/weakness/resistance/reduction/dealt/damage` — see `attack.ts:282-296`) plus the resulting `active?.damage`. For the conditional card you'll also want a case where the attacker has FEWER/EQUAL prizes so `bonus` is absent (assert `dealt?.bonus` is `undefined` and dealt stays at base).

## 8. Web/HUD surface

**Damage bonuses do NOT surface in the web app — this slice is engine-only.** The only passive the web projection reads is the HP one: `src/features/game/projection.ts:40` imports `effectiveMaxHp` and uses it at `:262` (`hp: effectiveMaxHp(state, pokemon)`). It does **not** import `passivesOf`, and there is no damage-preview / damage-bonus / Tool-damage-tooltip field anywhere in `projection.ts`. `damageBonusBeforeWR` / `damageReductionAfterWR` are purely engine-internal (surfaced only through the `DAMAGE_DEALT` log event → `packages/engine/src/log.ts`, not a projection field). The `GameHud.tsx` tooltips (`:81`, `:119`, `:173`, `:189`) are for `trainerPlayableIf` play-gate greying and activated-Ability buttons — unrelated to passive damage. Demo-deck comments (`src/features/game/demoDecks.ts:79`) merely list Vitality Band; not a runtime surface.

**Bottom line for wiring Defiance Band:** add a conditional variant of the existing `damageBonusBeforeWR` field to `PassiveEffects` (`registry.ts:91`) carrying a `BoardCondition`; author `sv01-169` in the id map (near `registry.ts:1574`, beside `VITALITY_BAND`); evaluate the condition with `conditionHolds(next, action.seat, cond)` at the pre-W/R `bonus` read in `attack.ts:271` (and mirror it in `interpreter.ts:1315` for `snipeActive`), since `passivesOf` currently lacks the attacker seat needed to evaluate the predicate. Choice Belt (`sv02-176`) is a *different* shape (a target-type gate "…Active Pokémon V", not a `BoardCondition`) and can be left for its own slice. No web changes required. **Key architectural note for the conditional shape:** `passivesOf(state, pokemon)` takes only `state` + the Pokémon — it has **no seat and no condition context**, and it aggregates all sources into flat sums. A conditional bonus therefore cannot be expressed by summing a plain number inside `passivesOf` unless you either (a) thread the owning `Seat` into `passivesOf` so it can call `conditionHolds`, or (b) add a new field carrying the `BoardCondition` and evaluate it at the two read sites that DO know the attacker's seat (`attack.ts:271` has `action.seat`; `interpreter.ts:1315` has `ctx.seat`). See Q5 for seat availability.

## 5. The `BoardCondition` vocabulary

**Union definition** — `packages/engine/src/effects.ts:156-168`:
```ts
export type BoardCondition =
  | { kind: "morePrizesThanOpponent" }   // :160  (comment :157-159 names Defiance Band explicitly)
  | { kind: "yourStadiumInPlay" }        // :164
  | { kind: "noEnergyOnYourPokemon" };   // :168
```
The comment at `effects.ts:157-159` already earmarks this member for Defiance Band. `BoardCondition` is imported into `interpreter.ts:18`.

**`conditionHolds`** — `interpreter.ts:1011-1023` (signature takes `GameState`, `Seat`, `BoardCondition`):
```ts
export function conditionHolds(state: GameState, seat: Seat, cond: BoardCondition): boolean {
  switch (cond.kind) {
    case "morePrizesThanOpponent":
      return state.players[seat].prizes.length > state.players[otherSeat(seat)].prizes.length; // :1014
    …
```

**`conditionNote`** (the printed-text describer) — also in `interpreter.ts`, `:1027-1036`:
```ts
export function conditionNote(cond: BoardCondition): string {
  switch (cond.kind) {
    case "morePrizesThanOpponent":
      return "you have more Prize cards remaining than your opponent"; // :1030
    …
```

**Seat access from the damage calc:** Yes. `attack(state, action)` has the full `GameState` (`next`) and both seats — `action.seat` is the attacker, `defenderSeat = otherSeat(action.seat)` (`attack.ts:160`). So `conditionHolds(next, action.seat, { kind: "morePrizesThanOpponent" })` evaluates the condition for the *attacking* seat directly at the `attack.ts:271` hook. The `snipeActive` mirror at `interpreter.ts:1305-1315` has `ctx.seat` (the attacker) and `state`, so it can call `conditionHolds(state, ctx.seat, …)` the same way. `passivesOf` itself does **not** receive a seat today (`continuous.ts:39`), so the condition must be evaluated at those call sites (or a seat threaded in).

## 7. Test conventions for passives

Two representative files to mirror:
- **`packages/engine/src/stadiumTool.test.ts:279-313`** — `describe("Vitality Band — +10 damage before Weakness/Resistance")`. This is the **direct analog** for Defiance Band (a Tool with a pre-W/R additive). It builds a board with `p1Turn2(6)`, sets actives via `setActiveFromDeck(state, "p1", "fix-attacker")` / `"fix-wall"` / `"fix-weak"`, pays cost with `attachFromDeck(…, "fix-energy", 1)`, draws the Tool with `handFromDeck(state,"p1","sv01-197",1)` + `handUid`, attaches via `applyAction(…, { type:"attachTool", seat:"p1", uid, target:{spot:"active"} })`, attacks with `mustApply(state, { type:"attack", seat:"p1", index:0 })`, then asserts on the `DAMAGE_DEALT` event via `find(events,"DAMAGE_DEALT")`: `expect(dealt?.base).toBe(30); expect(dealt?.bonus).toBe(10); expect(dealt?.dealt).toBe(40)`. The `:298-312` case pins the **before-W/R** ordering: `(30+10)×2 = 80` against `fix-weak` (a wrong after-W/R impl would give 70).
- **`packages/engine/src/coverage.test.ts:141-159`** — the reduction analog, using `covBoard(n)` + the `bite` attack action + `find(events,"DAMAGE_DEALT")` `.toMatchObject({ base, reduction, dealt })` + `after.players.p2.active?.damage`.

**Fixtures/helpers** are all in `packages/engine/src/testFixtures.ts`: board builders `p1Turn2` / `covBoard(n)` (n = a per-suite deck-count key, see the count tables ~`:1616-2252`); `setActiveFromDeck` (`:2276`), `attachFromDeck` (`:2486`), `handFromDeck` (`:2550`), `handUid` (`:2404`), `handUids` (`:2412`), `must` (`:2351`), `mustApply` (`:2357`). Battler fixtures: `fix-attacker` (`:145`, its "Bite" costs `[C]`, base 30), `fix-wall` (120 HP, `:211`), `fix-weak` (60 HP, ×2 Fire, `:213`). Damage is asserted off the emitted `DAMAGE_DEALT` GameEvent (fields `base/scaled/bonus/weakness/resistance/reduction/dealt/damage` — see `attack.ts:282-296`) plus the resulting `active?.damage`. For the conditional card you'll also want a case where the attacker has FEWER/EQUAL prizes so `bonus` is absent (assert `dealt?.bonus` is `undefined` and dealt stays at base).

## 8. Web/HUD surface

**Damage bonuses do NOT surface in the web app — this slice is engine-only.** The only passive the web projection reads is the HP one: `src/features/game/projection.ts:40` imports `effectiveMaxHp` and uses it at `:262` (`hp: effectiveMaxHp(state, pokemon)`). It does **not** import `passivesOf`, and there is no damage-preview / damage-bonus / Tool-damage-tooltip field anywhere in `projection.ts`. `damageBonusBeforeWR` / `damageReductionAfterWR` are purely engine-internal (surfaced only through the `DAMAGE_DEALT` log event → `packages/engine/src/log.ts`, not a projection field). The `GameHud.tsx` tooltips (`:81`, `:119`, `:173`, `:189`) are for `trainerPlayableIf` play-gate greying and activated-Ability buttons — unrelated to passive damage. Demo-deck comments (`src/features/game/demoDecks.ts:79`) merely list Vitality Band; not a runtime surface.

**Bottom line for wiring Defiance Band:** add a conditional variant of the existing `damageBonusBeforeWR` field to `PassiveEffects` (`registry.ts:91`) carrying a `BoardCondition`; author `sv01-169` in the id map (near `registry.ts:1574`, beside `VITALITY_BAND`); evaluate the condition with `conditionHolds(next, action.seat, cond)` at the pre-W/R `bonus` read in `attack.ts:271` (and mirror it in `interpreter.ts:1315` for `snipeActive`), since `passivesOf` currently lacks the attacker seat needed to evaluate the predicate. Choice Belt (`sv02-176`) is a *different* shape (a target-type gate "…Active Pokémon V", not a `BoardCondition`) and can be left for its own slice. No web changes required. server-side hidden-information filter the lobby Durable Object runs once per
    connected socket, so no full `GameState` (opponent hand/deck/prizes) ever
    crosses the network. It restates the web app's playmat redaction (opponent
    hand/prizes/decks as counts, setup in-play as anonymous backs) against the
    neutral `@luminous/schema` `RedactedGame` wire shape — no image URLs, no
    engine imports on the far side. Its subtle phase derivation (turn owner /
    who-must-act / parked interrupt / outcome) is the exhaustive `phaseViewOf`
    switch, MOVED here from that projection (phaseView.ts) so both share one
    source; the web projection now imports it. No game-logic change — this slice
    adds a read surface, not a rule.

    0.41.0 — CONCEDE (P4 online, increment 3c-ii). The first change to the win
    vocabulary since M1: `GameOverReason` gains **`conceded`** and a new
    `concede(state, action)` (flow.ts, beside `finishGame`) hands the game to the
    opponent. Unlike every other action it is legal in ANY phase but `gameOver` —
    a concede that only worked on your own turn would be useless in the situations
    it exists for (an opponent who walked away mid-turn, a park nobody can answer),
    and it is the one action that can always END a match that is otherwise stuck.
    ONE reason covers both triggers — a player pressing concede, and the P4 server
    forfeiting for a player who abandoned an online match — because to the opponent
    they are the same event, and the engine has no business knowing about sockets.
    This IS a rules-surface change (a new way a game can end), hence the minor
    bump; the two reason→prose maps (log.ts `GAME_OVER_REASONS`, the web's
    `GAME_OVER_DETAIL`) became total Records in the same pass, so a future reason
    is a compile error rather than silently rendering as "the deck ran out". */
export const engineVersion = "0.41.0";
