// @luminous/engine — deterministic, pure PTCG game engine (P3).
//
// M1 surface: the setup sequence (shuffle, coin flip, hands + mulligans +
// compensation, placements, prizes), the turn loop with its mandatory draw
// and deck-out loss, energy attach, bench plays, retreat and pass. M2 adds
// the attack step: costs, weakness/resistance damage, Knock Outs with prize
// taking and forced promotion, and the full §14 win check — resolved through
// a staged turn tail that can park on player decisions. M3 adds the Special
// Conditions (§12) with their attack/retreat gates and the confusion flip,
// the Pokémon Checkup (§13) with its ticks, recoveries and KOs, and the
// first text-derived attack effects (effects.ts). M4 begins with evolution
// (§10): an Evolution card placed on an in-play Pokémon whose top card it
// evolves from, carrying over damage/energy/tools and clearing Special
// Conditions, under the §4/§10 timing rules. Spec:
// docs/workstreams/simulator.md; ruleset: docs/reference/ptcg-rules.md.
// Everything is (state, action) → result: no classes, no wall clock, no
// unseeded randomness — the same seed and actions replay identically. The
// package is shared by the web app (local play + the semantic animation
// event stream) and the api Worker (authoritative online matches, P4).

import type { ApplyResult, GameAction } from "./actions";
import { err } from "./actions";
import { attack, promote, takePrizes } from "./attack";
import { attachTool, playTrainer, rareCandy, resolveEffect, useAbility } from "./cardplay";
import { concede } from "./flow";
import {
  chooseFirstPlayer,
  setupDrawExtra,
  setupPlaceActive,
  setupPlaceBench,
  setupReady,
} from "./setup";
import { attachEnergy, endTurn, evolve, playBasicToBench, retreat } from "./turn";
import type { GameState, Seat } from "./types";

/** Engine milestone marker (M5 op-slice: **`attachFromTop`** — the from-the-top
    ATTACH the lookAtTopN slice deferred. Look at the top N of your own deck and
    attach the Energy you find there straight onto your Pokémon, "**in any way you
    like**" — so each attached card names its OWN destination, and the answer is a
    MAP (card → Pokémon) rather than the flat list every other card prompt takes
    (the new `attachCards` prompt). Two consumers differing in every rider the op
    has: **Electric Generator** (Item — top 5, up to 2 Basic {L} Energy CARDS, onto
    your BENCHED {L} Pokémon) and **Hydreigon "Tri Howl"** (Ability, once per turn
    — top 3, ANY number of Energy cards, onto ANY of your Pokémon).

    The leftovers clause is the design point: "Shuffle the other cards back" is a
    trailing `shuffleDeck` op (those cards never left the deck), but "**Discard**
    the other cards" must name exactly the looked-at cards that were not attached,
    so it is `discardRest` ON the op — and it fires on the whiff and the decline
    too, which is the difference between Tri Howl costing three cards and costing
    nothing. The filter reads the PRINT (`basicEnergy` / `anyEnergy`), never
    `providesEnergy`: these cards sit in a DECK, attached to nothing (§6.5).
    providesEnergy was 0.24.0; the discardEnergy attack arms 0.23.0;
    attackEpilogue/park 0.22.0; discardEnergy 0.21.0; board conditions 0.20.0).

    **0.26.0 — `payFromHand`, the printed COST that parks.** "You can use
    this card only if you discard 2 OTHER cards from your hand" (Ultra Ball,
    Earthen Vessel) and "You must discard a card from your hand in order to use
    this Ability" (Tinkaton, Revavroom, Meowscarada ex, Radiant Blastoise) are ONE
    mechanism in two printed wordings — and the "other" appears exactly when the
    paying card is itself in the hand, which is why the play GATE excludes the
    played uid and the op carries no flag. It is the FIRST op of its program, so
    the payment happens before what it buys: Revavroom pays, THEN draws to a hand
    size that counts the payment. MANDATORY and exact, so `chooseCards` gained a
    `min` (0 for every printed "up to", `count` here — the one park with no
    decline) and a `"discard"` destination; `AbilityProgram.cost` is GONE, its one
    consumer migrated onto the op it was the fungible special case of.

    **0.27.0 — the printed number is a FLOOR, and the cost that is not a
    discard.** Two mandatory-exactly-N fixes, one on each prompt that could
    already say "up to". (1) `choosePokemonMulti` gained `min`/`max` +
    `declinable`: "put 3 damage counters on **1** of your opponent's Benched
    Pokémon" is not "up to 1", so Meowscarada ex / Radiant Blastoise can no longer
    pay an irreversible hand cost and then place nothing, while Hawlucha's printed
    "**you may** choose 2" stays all-or-nothing — 2 or none, never 1 of 2 — which
    is a decline the framework's auto-fired triggers leave nowhere else to live.
    (2) `discardFromHandCost` became **`payFromHand`** with a required
    destination: `to: "deckBottom"` pays UNDER THE DECK, landing **Dendra** ×3
    ("Put a card from your hand on the bottom of your deck. If you do, draw cards
    until you have 5") — nothing is discarded, yet the mechanism is the same
    mandatory pick, the same conditional benefit and the same printed play gate,
    which Dendra states as its contrapositive. HAND_COST_PAID carries `to`,
    because a payment to the discard becomes public and one to the deck never
    does. **Skwovet** ×2 ("Nest Stash") reaches the same destination with the
    WHOLE hand and needed no new op at all — `handRefresh` with Iono's `toBottom`
    + `onlyIfAnyMoved`.

    **0.28.0 — a clause can read what an earlier clause DID (§9.2).** The
    engine's first op→op data flow: an op files the uids it moved under a named
    `EffectSlot`, and a later op in the same program reads them. Two readers, one
    record — the printed "in this way" / "if you do" is a new `recordGate` (the
    third and last gate, spliced like the other two), and "you can't choose a card
    you discarded with the effect of this card" is `discardPileRetrieval.exclude`.
    Lands **Miriam** ×3 and **Superior Energy Retrieval** ×2, and lets **Dendra**
    finally say its own "if you do". The record rides `EffectContinuation`, NOT
    `EffectContext`: it is an accumulator, sibling to `rest`, where the context is
    a constant. And it is keyed by SLOT rather than by position — Miriam shuffles
    the deck between the retrieval and the sentence about it, so "the previous op"
    would have been wrong on the very first card that needed this.

    0.29.0 — `attachFromDeck`: SEARCH your deck for Energy and attach it straight
    onto your Pokémon, the deck-search sibling of `attachFromTop`. It shares that
    op's `attachCards` MAP prompt (the printed clause is the same one) and differs
    only where the SOURCE forces it to: the candidate set is the whole deck, so it
    is COLLAPSED to `max` representatives per interchangeable class (D42's rule —
    a real list holds a dozen Basic {R}), and there is no leftovers clause, so the
    printed "Then, shuffle your deck" is the usual trailing `shuffleDeck`. Two
    printed target rules, one new field: "in any way you like" (**Charizard ex**
    ×4, an onEvolve trigger) is no rider at all, and "for each of those Pokémon"
    (**Janine's Secret Art** ×2) is `maxPerTarget: 1`. Janine also extends §9.2 —
    `recordGate.contains` narrows the gate from "did the earlier op do anything"
    to "did anything land on your ACTIVE", which is what her printed self-poison
    turns on.

    0.30.0 — `EffectContext.sourceUid`: the context now names the Pokémon whose
    effect is running — the printed "this Pokémon" — set at every run site that
    knows it (an activated Ability's own Pokémon, a trigger's, the attacker) and
    ABSENT for a Trainer program, which has no such Pokémon. Constant for the
    run, rides the continuation across parks (JSON, D14). First reader:
    `attachFromDeck.toSelf`, the third printed target rule ("attach it to THIS
    Pokémon"), which lands **Pawmot** ×2 ("Electrogenesis") — a benched Pawmot
    feeds ITSELF, the exact sentence no seat-relative target rule could say.

    0.31.0 — `healChosen.upTo`: the printed "up to N … each" heal (Saguaro ×3,
    "Choose up to 2 of your Pokémon and heal 50 damage from each of them") —
    the first consumer of choosePokemonMulti's min: 0 end (§9.1's "up to"
    legalizes 0..max), parked at every non-empty board with §8.6 clamping the
    ask.

    0.32.0 — `bottomFromOpponentHand` + `opponentMayDraw`: the opponent reveals
    their hand (a new public HAND_REVEALED — every uid, because that is what
    the printed word means), the controller bottoms a chosen card onto the
    OPPONENT's deck (CARD_TO_BOTTOM_OF_DECK, named — the whole move happened
    face up), and the gated draw is the engine's first decision ANSWERED BY THE
    NON-CONTROLLER: the park carries a decider, the phase an `answerer` (absent
    when it is the controller, so every older park is byte-identical), and
    resolveEffect admits only that seat. Ortega ×2 authored (the Miriam shape
    across the table), Greavard "Underworld Stroll" DERIVED (the Supporter-
    filtered attack twin — its second attack is why the card-level registry
    `attack` field could not carry it). programPlayable gains the public-count
    empty-opponent-hand gate (the Catcher/Hammer class) and is now EXPORTED —
    the HUD greys with the predicate that rejects.

    0.33.0 — `damageSelf` + the TWO-seat attack epilogue: the recoil clause "This
    Pokémon also does N damage to itself" (Skeledirge sv01-038 "Blazing Shout")
    is the engine's first attack that damages its OWN board, placed flat as
    COUNTERS_PLACED source "self" (the confusion self-hit's model, OUTSIDE the
    §8.5 W/R pipeline). finishAttack's KO sweep widened from the single defender
    seat to BOTH, in [defender, attacker] order so §8.1's "the player whose turn
    it is takes their Prizes first" holds, and a self-KO prizes to the defender.
    This makes the §14 double-KO tie reachable from the attack path for the first
    time — collectKnockOuts' existing speculative guard owns it (the D42 debt,
    paid).

    0.34.0 — count-scaled attack damage (the additive "+" family): the printed
    "This attack does N more damage for each damage counter on this Pokémon"
    (Paldean Tauros sv02-028 "Raging Horns", fix-attacker "Rage") is now SIMULATED
    — `deriveAttackDamageBonus` folds N × (the attacker's OWN damage counters) into
    the base BEFORE the §8.5 W/R pipeline (attack.ts), alongside the continuous
    Vitality Band bonus. The new DAMAGE_DEALT `scaled` field carries it (present
    only when it applied), and the "+"/text is no longer flagged loudly for these
    cards. Charizard ex sv03-125 "Burning Darkness" (a DIFFERENT count source — the
    opponent's taken Prizes) STAYS on the ATTACK_EFFECT_SKIPPED path, the
    anchor-guard witness proving the deriver is narrow.

    0.35.0 — the count union's SECOND member: Charizard ex sv03-125 "Burning
    Darkness" (180+, "… for each Prize card your opponent has taken") now SIMULATES,
    folding 30 × (the opponent's TAKEN Prizes = 6 − their remaining pile) into the
    base. `scaledAttackDamage` widened to reach the opponent's board; the
    unsimulated-"+" witness moved to Entei sv03-030 (an attached-Energy count
    source, still no reader). The "×"/multiply Prize family (Pecharunt ex — no
    "more") stays loud.

    0.36.0 — the "×"/multiply damage family, the additive family's sibling: "This
    attack does N damage for each Prize card your opponent has taken." (NO "more" —
    Pecharunt ex sv06.5-039 60×, Annihilape sv01-109 70×) now SIMULATES. It reuses
    the additive family's `opponentPrizesTaken` count evaluator UNCHANGED via a new
    reader `deriveAttackDamageMultiplier`; the only difference is the fold — the
    printed "N×" base is the per-unit, so it is DROPPED and `per × count` is the
    WHOLE damage (count 0 → 0 damage), where the additive family adds `per × count`
    onto a printed base. Wo-Chien ex (benched-target) and Chien-Pao ex
    (discarded-Energy count) stay loud, the anchor-guard witnesses.

    0.37.0 — the "×"/multiply family's benched-TARGET sibling: Wo-Chien ex sv02-027
    "Covetous Ivy" ("This attack does 60 damage to 1 of your opponent's Benched
    Pokémon for each Prize card your opponent has taken.") now SIMULATES. Its target
    is one CHOSEN Benched Pokémon rather than the Defender, so it is NOT the pre-W/R
    Defender fold (D56) but a `damageChosen` op — the put-counter snipe (Hawlucha /
    Meowscarada) extended with `deals` (ATTACK DAMAGE, a DAMAGE_DEALT with the
    benched reduction passive, not a flat placed counter) and `perTakenPrize` (the
    amount is `60 × the opponent's taken Prizes`, read from state in the interpreter;
    0 taken → no damage and no pick). The "6 − remaining" Prize formula is now the
    shared `takenPrizes` helper (types.ts), used by both this and the D55/D56 fold.
    Chien-Pao ex "Hail Blade" (a DISCARDED-Energy count, and a PRE-damage park) stays
    loud, the remaining "×" sibling.

    0.38.0 — the flat benched-snipe RIDER family: "This attack ALSO does N damage to 1
    of your opponent's Benched Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for
    Benched Pokémon.)" now SIMULATES — a SECONDARY snipe after the main damage (which
    rides the attack's own `damage` field). It is the SAME count-1 `deals` snipe as
    D57's Covetous Ivy WITHOUT `perTakenPrize` (a fixed N, not Prize-scaled), so it is
    a new derive `ALSO_BENCHED_SNIPE` and ZERO new op/interpreter code. Lands ~15
    prints across Miraidon / Tadbulb / Pawmot / Bellibolt / Decidueye ex / Jumpluff /
    Orthworm / Palafin / Pyroar / Dartrix. Flamigo's "If Flamigo is on your Bench, …"
    (a board-condition gate) and the "each of" / "2 of" / "1 of YOUR Benched" variants
    stay loud, each a different shape.

    0.39.0 — the ANY-target snipe family: "This attack does N damage to 1 of your
    opponent's Pokémon." (the WHOLE attack — the Active OR a Bench) now SIMULATES.
    `damageChosen` gained a `target: "opponentAny"` mode (candidates = the opponent's
    Active + Bench, via `oppAnyRefs`), and `placeSnipe` an Active arm (`snipeActive`):
    a snipe that lands on the ACTIVE runs the §8.5 W/R pipeline (base → ×Weakness →
    −Resistance → −reduction), where a Benched target stays flat — the rules'
    "Weakness/Resistance apply only to the Active" made conditional on the pick.
    Fezandipiti ex sv06.5-038 "Cruel Arrow" (100), Rotom sv01-069 "Linear Attack"
    (20), Paldean Tauros "Aqua Dive", Bellibolt ex, Kilowattrel. Umbreon "Feint
    Attack" (a different W/R-immunity wording), Pawmot ex (a discard cost), and
    Magikarp (a coin flip) stay loud.

    0.40.0 — the authoritative per-viewer REDACTOR (P4 online, increment 1c). The
    engine gains `redactGame(state, seat) → RedactedGame` (redact.ts): the PURE
    server-side hidden-information filter the lobby Durable Object runs once per
    connected socket, so no full `GameState` (opponent hand/deck/prizes) ever
    crosses the network. It restates the web app's playmat redaction (opponent
    hand/prizes/decks as counts, setup in-play as anonymous backs) against the
    neutral `@luminous/schema` `RedactedGame` wire shape — no image URLs, no
    engine imports on the far side. Its subtle phase derivation (turn owner /
    who-must-act / parked interrupt / outcome) is the exhaustive `phaseViewOf`
    switch, MOVED here from that projection (phaseView.ts) so both share one
    source; the web projection now imports it. No game-logic change — this slice
    adds a read surface, not a rule.

    0.41.0 — CONCEDE (P4 online, increment 3c-ii). The first change to the win
    vocabulary since M1: `GameOverReason` gains **`conceded`** and a new
    `concede(state, action)` (flow.ts, beside `finishGame`) hands the game to the
    opponent. Unlike every other action it is legal in ANY phase but `gameOver` —
    a concede that only worked on your own turn would be useless in the situations
    it exists for (an opponent who walked away mid-turn, a park nobody can answer),
    and it is the one action that can always END a match that is otherwise stuck.
    ONE reason covers both triggers — a player pressing concede, and the P4 server
    forfeiting for a player who abandoned an online match — because to the opponent
    they are the same event, and the engine has no business knowing about sockets.
    This IS a rules-surface change (a new way a game can end), hence the minor
    bump; the two reason→prose maps (log.ts `GAME_OVER_REASONS`, the web's
    `GAME_OVER_DETAIL`) became total Records in the same pass, so a future reason
    is a compile error rather than silently rendering as "the deck ran out". */

/** The one reducer. Dispatches on action type; each handler validates the
    phase and acting seat itself and returns ok/err without ever throwing
    or mutating its input.

    The two guards below are unreachable through the typed API but NOT through
    the wire: P4's authoritative Worker decodes actions from a client, and the
    never-throw contract has to hold for a bogus `type` or `seat` too (an
    unknown seat would otherwise index `players` with undefined and throw). */
export function applyAction(state: GameState, action: GameAction): ApplyResult {
  // A finished game accepts nothing further.
  if (state.phase.kind === "gameOver") {
    const outcome = state.phase.outcome;
    return err(
      "GAME_OVER",
      outcome.result === "win"
        ? `the game is over (${outcome.winner} won: ${outcome.reason})`
        : "the game is over (tie)",
    );
  }
  if (!isSeat(action.seat)) {
    return err("UNKNOWN_SEAT", `"${String(action.seat)}" is not a seat`);
  }
  switch (action.type) {
    case "chooseFirstPlayer":
      return chooseFirstPlayer(state, action);
    case "setupDrawExtra":
      return setupDrawExtra(state, action);
    case "setupPlaceActive":
      return setupPlaceActive(state, action);
    case "setupPlaceBench":
      return setupPlaceBench(state, action);
    case "setupReady":
      return setupReady(state, action);
    case "attachEnergy":
      return attachEnergy(state, action);
    case "playBasicToBench":
      return playBasicToBench(state, action);
    case "evolve":
      return evolve(state, action);
    case "rareCandy":
      return rareCandy(state, action);
    case "retreat":
      return retreat(state, action);
    case "attack":
      return attack(state, action);
    case "playTrainer":
      return playTrainer(state, action);
    case "attachTool":
      return attachTool(state, action);
    case "useAbility":
      return useAbility(state, action);
    case "resolveEffect":
      return resolveEffect(state, action);
    case "takePrizes":
      return takePrizes(state, action);
    case "promote":
      return promote(state, action);
    case "endTurn":
      return endTurn(state, action);
    case "concede":
      return concede(state, action);
    default:
      return err("UNKNOWN_ACTION", `unknown action type "${(action as { type: string }).type}"`);
  }
}

function isSeat(value: unknown): value is Seat {
  return value === "p1" || value === "p2";
}

# Simulator coverage — the new-op backlog (P3-M5)

The engine simulates cards as **data-driven op programs** (registry.ts). A card
is playable when its printed effect maps onto the op vocabulary
(`effects.ts` EffectOp, plus the continuous/energy/ability shapes in
`registry.ts`). M4 built the vocabulary through nine slices; M5 expands **card
coverage** across the SV-era pool.

## Method — a classify → verify Workflow fan-out (2026-07-19)
The 140 un-authored **sv01–sv03** Trainers (61), Special Energies (4) and
Pokémon Abilities (75) were classified by a 10-agent fan-out (5 batches ×
classify + adversarial verify), each card judged against the current op
vocabulary with the deriver doctrine — **exact map or flag** (a wrong-but-plausible
program is worse than a flag). Every authorable program was then hand-verified
against the local catalog before landing.

## Result
| Verdict | Count |
|---|---|
| **authorable now** (landed this pass) | **5** |
| needs a new op (backlog below) | 113 |
| already authored (M4) | 22 |
| **total classified** | 140 |

Only ~4% of the un-authored pool is expressible with today's ops — coverage is
**op-bound, not authoring-bound**: each new primitive unlocks a whole family, so
the backlog below (ranked by cards-unlocked) is the roadmap for the next slices.
Authoring is then a few registry rows per card, exactly as D8 intended.

### Authored this pass (M5 #1)
| Card | id | Program |
|---|---|---|
| Poké Ball | sv01-185 | Item — `coinFlipGate → [searchDeck anyPokemon→hand, shuffleDeck]` |
| Pokémon Catcher | sv01-187 | Item — `coinFlipGate → [gust]` |
| Nemona | sv01-180 | Supporter — `drawCards 3` |
| Copperajah ex (Bronze Body) | sv02-150 | passive `damageReductionAfterWR: 30` |
| Stonjourner (Exoskeleton) | sv01-121 | passive `damageReductionAfterWR: 20` |

(The fan-out mis-placed Poké Ball's `shuffleDeck` *after* the coin gate — it must
be *inside* it, or a tails play reorders the deck; fixed + pinned by a test.)

## New-op backlog — ranked by cards unlocked (sv01–03)
Build these to expand coverage; the count is how many classified cards each
unblocks. High-value ops first.

| New op / capability | Cards | Example cards |
|---|---:|---|
| 🚧 **`attachEnergyFrom`** (attach Energy from hand/discard/deck to a chosen Pokémon) | 11 | **DONE 4/11: Quaquaval, Baxcalibur** (single attach from hand/discard, engine 0.12.0) + **Gardevoir ex** (the `targetType`/`bonusCounters`/`notIfKO` riders, engine 0.13.0) + **Koraidon ex "Dino Cry"** (multi-attach = N ops + `basicOnly` + the `endsTurn` fold, engine 0.14.0). Remaining 7 need MORE ops on top: Forretress ex (deck-search + self-KO), Charizard ex (onEvolve + deck-search-multi), Geeta (deck-search + can't-attack), Electric Generator/Hydreigon (need `lookAtTopN`), Pawmot (deck-search→self, needs the source uid in EffectContext), Wigglytuff (a Special Energy by name) |
| ✅ **`discardPileRetrieval`** (put/shuffle cards from discard → hand/deck) | 6 | **DONE 5/6** — engine 0.15.0 landed the core (the searchDeck mirror + `supporter`/`pokemonOrBasicEnergy` filters): **Energy Retrieval** (2 Basic Energy → hand), **Pal Pad** (2 Supporters → deck), **Super Rod** (3 Pokémon/Basic Energy → deck); engine 0.28.0's §9.2 op→op record landed the two that had to read their own earlier clause: **Superior Energy Retrieval** ×2 (the new `exclude` rider — the cost pays INTO this pile, so without it the payment refunds itself) and **Miriam** ×3 (the new `recordAs` rider + a `recordGate` two ops downstream). Remaining 1: **Pelipper** (an Ability, not a Trainer). |
| ✅ **`lookAtTopN`** (reveal/take a matching card from the top N) | 5 | **DONE 2/5** (engine 0.16.0, the top-of-deck twin of searchDeck: candidates are the top-N matches, then a trailing shuffle): **Great Ball** (top 7 → a Pokémon), **Pokégear 3.0** (top 7 → a Supporter). Remaining 3 need MORE: Electric Generator + Hydreigon attach the found Energy (a from-the-top **attach** variant — the 2 attachEnergyFrom cards this also unblocks), Malamar peeks at the OPPONENT's deck top (a distinct info-only op). |
| ✅ **`moveEnergy`** (move an Energy between your Pokémon) | 5 | **DONE 3/5** (engine 0.17.0, the compound-park own→own op + the `anyEnergy` filter): **Energy Switch** (a Basic Energy, max 1), **Poppy** (up to 2 any Energy, max 2), and — engine 0.24.0, the `route: "benchToActive"` rider + the `providesEnergy` filter — **Armarouge** "Fire Off" (a {R} Energy benched→Active, as often as you like). | ✅ **the discardEnergy ATTACK arms** — the opponent-side twins + the exact-N count | 11 | **DONE (engine 0.23.0), again with ZERO registry rows — two deriver sentences and one widened field.** The **twins** ("Discard an Energy from your opponent's Active Pokémon.", bare and behind a flip) run the EXISTING `opponentActive` arm with an `anyEnergy` filter: **Pincurchin** (sv02-072), **Gumshoos** (sv03-177), **Dragonite V ×2** (swsh10.5-049/-076); **Dedenne** (sv01-094), **Maschiff** (sv01-136), **Tympole** (sv03-050), **Yveltal** (sv06.5-035). The **exact-N** self-discard widens `count` from `"all"` to any number: **Corviknight** (sv02-148), **Slither Wing** (sv06.5-026), **Koraidon** (sv01-124). The prompt's `scope` became `{kind:"total",count} \| {kind:"each"}` and the interchangeable collapse now keeps `count` reps per class. STILL BLOCKED after it: the **TYPED** discards (closed by the row below), the multi-sentence riders (**Sandaconda**, **Eiscue ex**, **Weavile**), and **Krookodile**'s flip-until-tails repeat count. |
| ✅ **the `providesEnergy` CardFilter** — "an Energy that PROVIDES {X}" | 7 | **DONE (engine 0.24.0) — the last missing piece of the energy-discard family, and the first filter a CARD alone cannot answer.** "{L} Energy" is not "a Basic Lightning card": a Special providing {L} IS one, a wildcard (Luminous) is one of EVERY type, and provision is a while-ATTACHED property that Luminous's own text makes depend on the holder's other attachments — so the predicate reads what an Energy gives ON ITS HOST, through the very code §8.2's cost matcher reads (`unitsProvidedBy`). `matchesFilter`, the deck/hand/discard scanner, answers FALSE for it (a card in a pile is attached to nothing), so authoring it into a pile-scanning op is a loud no-op rather than a wrong card. TWO consumers, one vocabulary (the D40 shape): the **typed self-discard**, DERIVED in both printed notations — the modern "{R}" and the swsh-era spelled-out "Fire" — for **Kilowattrel** (sv01-079), **Arcanine ex ×2** (sv01-032/-224), **Charmeleon** (swsh10.5-009) and **Charizard** (swsh10.5-010) with ZERO registry rows; and **`moveEnergy`'s `benchToActive` route**, authoring **Armarouge ×2** (sv01-041/-203). STILL BLOCKED, and now every one of them for sentence STRUCTURE rather than for any missing filter: **Pawmot ex** (a typed discard plus "220 damage to 1 of your opponent's Pokémon" — `damageChosen` exists but targets the Bench, not any Pokémon), **Bellibolt ex** ("you may … to make it Paralyzed" — an optional discard BUYING an effect), **Chien-Pao ex** / **Mewtwo VSTAR** (a variable count with damage scaling off it), **Sandaconda** / **Eiscue ex** / **Weavile** (rider clauses) and **Krookodile** (a repeat count). |

Two printed wordings, ONE mechanism, and the wording tracks where the paying card sits: TRAINERS say "only if you discard 2 **other** cards" because the card is in the hand it pays from — **Ultra Ball** (sv01-196), **Earthen Vessel** (sv06.5-096, "another card"); ABILITIES never say "other" because the card is on the board — **Revavroom** (sv01-142, "an Energy card" → draw to 6, the ORDER witness), **Tinkaton** (sv02-105, "a card" → draw 3, the unfiltered general case). | **`onDamagedByAttack`** (a trigger firing when damaged by an attack, even if KO'd) | 4 | Cacnea, Cacturne, Armarouge, Klawf ex |

| **`stadiumActivatedAbility`** (a "once during each player's turn" Stadium) | 3 | Artazon, Mesagoza, Town Store |
| **`damageAttacker`** (put counters on the attacking Pokémon) | 3 | Cacnea, Cacturne, Stunfisk |

**Long tail (~70 single-card ops)** — e.g. `bounceToHand` (Penny), `moveDamageCounters`
(Slowbro), `healBothPlayers` (Picnic Basket), `noRetreatCostAura` (Clefable ex),

# Simulator coverage — the new-op backlog (P3-M5)

The engine simulates cards as **data-driven op programs** (registry.ts). A card
is playable when its printed effect maps onto the op vocabulary
(`effects.ts` EffectOp, plus the continuous/energy/ability shapes in
`registry.ts`). M4 built the vocabulary through nine slices; M5 expands **card
coverage** across the SV-era pool.

## Method — a classify → verify Workflow fan-out (2026-07-19)
The 140 un-authored **sv01–sv03** Trainers (61), Special Energies (4) and
Pokémon Abilities (75) were classified by a 10-agent fan-out (5 batches ×
classify + adversarial verify), each card judged against the current op
vocabulary with the deriver doctrine — **exact map or flag** (a wrong-but-plausible
program is worse than a flag). Every authorable program was then hand-verified
against the local catalog before landing.

## Result
| Verdict | Count |
|---|---|
| **authorable now** (landed this pass) | **5** |
| needs a new op (backlog below) | 113 |
| already authored (M4) | 22 |
| **total classified** | 140 |

Only ~4% of the un-authored pool is expressible with today's ops — coverage is
**op-bound, not authoring-bound**: each new primitive unlocks a whole family, so
the backlog below (ranked by cards-unlocked) is the roadmap for the next slices.
Authoring is then a few registry rows per card, exactly as D8 intended.

### Authored this pass (M5 #1)
| Card | id | Program |
|---|---|---|
| Poké Ball | sv01-185 | Item — `coinFlipGate → [searchDeck anyPokemon→hand, shuffleDeck]` |
| Pokémon Catcher | sv01-187 | Item — `coinFlipGate → [gust]` |
| Nemona | sv01-180 | Supporter — `drawCards 3` |
| Copperajah ex (Bronze Body) | sv02-150 | passive `damageReductionAfterWR: 30` |
| Stonjourner (Exoskeleton) | sv01-121 | passive `damageReductionAfterWR: 20` |

(The fan-out mis-placed Poké Ball's `shuffleDeck` *after* the coin gate — it must
be *inside* it, or a tails play reorders the deck; fixed + pinned by a test.)

## New-op backlog — ranked by cards unlocked (sv01–03)
Build these to expand coverage; the count is how many classified cards each
unblocks. High-value ops first.

Remaining 7 need MORE ops on top: Forretress ex (deck-search + self-KO), Charizard ex (onEvolve + deck-search-multi), Geeta (deck-search + can't-attack), Electric Generator/Hydreigon (need `lookAtTopN`), Pawmot (deck-search→self, needs the source uid in EffectContext), Wigglytuff (a Special Energy by name) |

The **exact-N** self-discard widens `count` from `"all"` to any number: **Corviknight** (sv02-148), **Slither Wing** (sv06.5-026), **Koraidon** (sv01-124). The prompt's `scope` became `{kind:"total",count} \| {kind:"each"}` and the interchangeable collapse now keeps `count` reps per class. STILL BLOCKED after it: the **TYPED** discards (closed by the row below), the multi-sentence riders (**Sandaconda**, **Eiscue ex**, **Weavile**), and **Krookodile**'s flip-until-tails repeat count. |

TWO consumers, one vocabulary (the D40 shape): the **typed self-discard**, DERIVED in both printed notations — the modern "{R}" and the swsh-era spelled-out "Fire" — for **Kilowattrel** (sv01-079), **Arcanine ex ×2** (sv01-032/-224), **Charmeleon** (swsh10.5-009) and **Charizard** (swsh10.5-010) with ZERO registry rows; and **`moveEnergy`'s `benchToActive` route**, authoring **Armarouge ×2** (sv01-041/-203). 1. ✅ **`attachEnergyFrom`** — the single biggest unlock (11+, and the engine of most

   (Exp. Share). Next candidates: the from-the-top **attach** variant (Electric
   Generator / Hydreigon, also 2 attachEnergyFrom cards), the **`conditionalPlay`**

   Katy — **plus Judge**, the first op to affect the OPPONENT's hand/deck; and it
   closes the `endTurn` row via the Trainer-path `trainerEndsTurn` fold; then engine
   0.19.0 added **Iono** as three riders — `toBottom` (deck order survives),
   `prizeCount` draw, `onlyIfAnyMoved` gate). No Marnie in the sv01–03 catalog.

tests + review), and each turns dozens of "needs-op" rows into a few data rows.

# Simulator coverage — the new-op backlog (P3-M5)

The engine simulates cards as **data-driven op programs** (registry.ts). A card
is playable when its printed effect maps onto the op vocabulary
(`effects.ts` EffectOp, plus the continuous/energy/ability shapes in
`registry.ts`). M4 built the vocabulary through nine slices; M5 expands **card
coverage** across the SV-era pool.

## Method — a classify → verify Workflow fan-out (2026-07-19)
The 140 un-authored **sv01–sv03** Trainers (61), Special Energies (4) and
Pokémon Abilities (75) were classified by a 10-agent fan-out (5 batches ×
classify + adversarial verify), each card judged against the current op
vocabulary with the deriver doctrine — **exact map or flag** (a wrong-but-plausible
program is worse than a flag). Every authorable program was then hand-verified
against the local catalog before landing.

## Result
| Verdict | Count |
|---|---|
| **authorable now** (landed this pass) | **5** |
| needs a new op (backlog below) | 113 |
| already authored (M4) | 22 |
| **total classified** | 140 |

Only ~4% of the un-authored pool is expressible with today's ops — coverage is
**op-bound, not authoring-bound**: each new primitive unlocks a whole family, so
the backlog below (ranked by cards-unlocked) is the roadmap for the next slices.
Authoring is then a few registry rows per card, exactly as D8 intended.

### Authored this pass (M5 #1)
| Card | id | Program |
|---|---|---|
| Poké Ball | sv01-185 | Item — `coinFlipGate → [searchDeck anyPokemon→hand, shuffleDeck]` |
| Pokémon Catcher | sv01-187 | Item — `coinFlipGate → [gust]` |
| Nemona | sv01-180 | Supporter — `drawCards 3` |
| Copperajah ex (Bronze Body) | sv02-150 | passive `damageReductionAfterWR: 30` |
| Stonjourner (Exoskeleton) | sv01-121 | passive `damageReductionAfterWR: 20` |

(The fan-out mis-placed Poké Ball's `shuffleDeck` *after* the coin gate — it must
be *inside* it, or a tails play reorders the deck; fixed + pinned by a test.)

## New-op backlog — ranked by cards unlocked (sv01–03)
Build these to expand coverage; the count is how many classified cards each
unblocks. High-value ops first.

Remaining 7 need MORE ops on top: Forretress ex (deck-search + self-KO), Charizard ex (onEvolve + deck-search-multi), Geeta (deck-search + can't-attack), Electric Generator/Hydreigon (need `lookAtTopN`), Pawmot (deck-search→self, needs the source uid in EffectContext), Wigglytuff (a Special Energy by name) |

Remaining 3 need MORE: Electric Generator + Hydreigon attach the found Energy (a from-the-top **attach** variant — the 2 attachEnergyFrom cards this also unblocks), Malamar peeks at the OPPONENT's deck top (a distinct info-only op). |

The prompt's `scope` became `{kind:"total",count} \| {kind:"each"}` and the interchangeable collapse now keeps `count` reps per class. STILL BLOCKED after it: the **TYPED** discards (closed by the row below), the multi-sentence riders (**Sandaconda**, **Eiscue ex**, **Weavile**), and **Krookodile**'s flip-until-tails repeat count. |
| ✅ **the `providesEnergy` CardFilter** — "an Energy that PROVIDES {X}" | 7 | **DONE (engine 0.24.0) — the last missing piece of the energy-discard family, and the first filter a CARD alone cannot answer.** "{L} Energy" is not "a Basic Lightning card": a Special providing {L} IS one, a wildcard (Luminous) is one of EVERY type, and provision is a while-ATTACHED property that Luminous's own text makes depend on the holder's other attachments — so the predicate reads what an Energy gives ON ITS HOST, through the very code §8.2's cost matcher reads (`unitsProvidedBy`). `matchesFilter`, the deck/hand/discard scanner, answers FALSE for it (a card in a pile is attached to nothing), so authoring it into a pile-scanning op is a loud no-op rather than a wrong card. TWO consumers, one vocabulary (the D40 shape): the **typed self-discard**, DERIVED in both printed notations — the modern "{R}" and the swsh-era spelled-out "Fire" — for **Kilowattrel** (sv01-079), **Arcanine ex ×2** (sv01-032/-224), **Charmeleon** (swsh10.5-009) and **Charizard** (swsh10.5-010) with ZERO registry rows; and **`moveEnergy`'s `benchToActive` route**, authoring **Armarouge ×2** (sv01-041/-203). STILL BLOCKED, and now every one of them for sentence STRUCTURE rather than for any missing filter: **Pawmot ex** (a typed discard plus "220 damage to 1 of your opponent's Pokémon" — `damageChosen` exists but targets the Bench, not any Pokémon), **Bellibolt ex** ("you may … to make it Paralyzed" — an optional discard BUYING an effect), **Chien-Pao ex** / **Mewtwo VSTAR** (a variable count with damage scaling off it), **Sandaconda** / **Eiscue ex** / **Weavile** (rider clauses) and **Krookodile** (a repeat count). |

# Simulator coverage — the new-op backlog (P3-M5)

The engine simulates cards as **data-driven op programs** (registry.ts). A card
is playable when its printed effect maps onto the op vocabulary
(`effects.ts` EffectOp, plus the continuous/energy/ability shapes in
`registry.ts`). M4 built the vocabulary through nine slices; M5 expands **card
coverage** across the SV-era pool.

## Method — a classify → verify Workflow fan-out (2026-07-19)
The 140 un-authored **sv01–sv03** Trainers (61), Special Energies (4) and
Pokémon Abilities (75) were classified by a 10-agent fan-out (5 batches ×
classify + adversarial verify), each card judged against the current op
vocabulary with the deriver doctrine — **exact map or flag** (a wrong-but-plausible
program is worse than a flag). Every authorable program was then hand-verified
against the local catalog before landing.

## Result
| Verdict | Count |
|---|---|
| **authorable now** (landed this pass) | **5** |
| needs a new op (backlog below) | 113 |
| already authored (M4) | 22 |
| **total classified** | 140 |

Only ~4% of the un-authored pool is expressible with today's ops — coverage is
**op-bound, not authoring-bound**: each new primitive unlocks a whole family, so
the backlog below (ranked by cards-unlocked) is the roadmap for the next slices.
Authoring is then a few registry rows per card, exactly as D8 intended.

### Authored this pass (M5 #1)
| Card | id | Program |
|---|---|---|
| Poké Ball | sv01-185 | Item — `coinFlipGate → [searchDeck anyPokemon→hand, shuffleDeck]` |
| Pokémon Catcher | sv01-187 | Item — `coinFlipGate → [gust]` |
| Nemona | sv01-180 | Supporter — `drawCards 3` |
| Copperajah ex (Bronze Body) | sv02-150 | passive `damageReductionAfterWR: 30` |
| Stonjourner (Exoskeleton) | sv01-121 | passive `damageReductionAfterWR: 20` |

(The fan-out mis-placed Poké Ball's `shuffleDeck` *after* the coin gate — it must
be *inside* it, or a tails play reorders the deck; fixed + pinned by a test.)

## New-op backlog — ranked by cards unlocked (sv01–03)

unblocks. High-value ops first.

The seven `glass.ts` constants that carry a transition — `GLASS_HUD_BUTTON`, `GLASS_GHOST_BUTTON`, `GLASS_DIALOG_GHOST_BUTTON`, `GLASS_ACCENT_BUTTON`, `GLASS_NEUTRAL_BUTTON`, `GLASS_FILTER_TOGGLE` (all `transition-all` + `active:scale-95`) and `GLASS_INPUT` (`transition-colors`) — each got `motion-reduce:transition-none` appended, so EVERY glass control app-wide (auth, lobby HUD, filters, decks, dialogs, corner controls) respects reduced motion from the constant rather than each call site; one additive edit covers the whole app. Under reduced motion the fade is off and the `active:scale-95` SNAPS rather than animating — the same behaviour `CoverDialog`'s `TILE_BASE` was browser-verified with in P5-8, so this is not a new interaction, only a wider one. **This REVERSES D88/D89's "patch at the call site" placement** for these constants; the reversal is deliberate and was named as the blessed next step in D89's own resume point, so it is a trailed reversal, not a silent one. With P5-10, P5's autonomous surface is exhausted: the only open P5 items (uploaded avatars, the remote P4 deploy) both need the user.* (2026-07-27) |

| D91 | Defiance Band — a CONDITIONAL passive damage bonus, the D40 `BoardCondition` vocabulary's third consumer (P3-M5, engine 0.42.0) | The `conditionalDamageBonus` backlog row's first card, and the first PASSIVE reader of the D40 vocabulary — the conditional twin of Vitality Band ("If you have more Prize cards remaining than your opponent, the attacks of the Pokémon this card is attached to do 30 more damage to your opponent's Active Pokémon (before applying Weakness and Resistance)", sv01-169). **A card row + one new field, not a new primitive**, because it REUSES the existing `morePrizesThanOpponent` condition (added at D40 and already read by Fighting Au Lait's play gate + a branch op — this is the same predicate as a passive). `PassiveEffects` gains **`damageBonusBeforeWRIf: { amount, cond: BoardCondition }`**. **The load-bearing design call: WHERE the condition is evaluated.** continuous.ts's `passivesOf` is the single continuous-modifier aggregation point but is SEAT-FREE (it takes only `state` + the Pokémon), and a `BoardCondition` is seat-relative (whose Prizes?). Folding the evaluation into `passivesOf` would have needed `conditionHolds` from interpreter.ts, and interpreter.ts already imports `passivesOf` — a MODULE CYCLE. So `passivesOf` stays pure and seat-free, now collecting the gated bonuses RAW in a new `conditionalDamageBonusBeforeWR: {amount,cond}[]` (aggregation is its job); the FOLD lives in a new **`interpreter.ts` `attackerPreWRBonus(state, pokemon, seat)`** (evaluation beside the sole `conditionHolds`, its job), shared by the ONLY two pre-W/R read sites — attack.ts's main hit (`action.seat`) and `snipeActive` (`ctx.seat`) — the only places that know the attacker's seat. Kept OUT of the unconditional `damageBonusBeforeWR` so the defender-reduction and HP reads (which never look at either) can never be credited an attacker's conditional bonus. **snipeActive parity is free**: it now calls the shared helper, so a snipe landing on the opponent's Active gets Defiance Band's +30 exactly as it already got Vitality Band's — verified by the existing Vitality Band snipe coverage still passing after the refactor. **Test-deck choice (a small but real call):** the new tests use a DEDICATED `DEFIANCE_DECK` fixture rather than adding sv01-169 to the shared `STADIUM_TOOL_DECK` — the latter is a fixed 60 (setup.ts enforces `DECK_SIZE`), so any card swapped in reshuffles every seed and broke a fragile opening-hand test (fix-energy-in-hand + fix-tool-in-deck) shared across 5 suites; a dedicated all-Basic deck is mulligan-free and seed-independent (cards pulled post-setup by id). **No web/API/DB/schema touch** — damage bonuses are engine-internal, surfaced only via the `DAMAGE_DEALT` log event (no projection field), confirmed by an Explore map. engineVersion 0.41.0 → **0.42.0**; 1941 → **1945** tests (registration + applies-when-behind + no-op-when-level + the (30+30)×2=120 before-W/R pin). `bun run check` green (137 files / 1945 tests). **Self-reviewed, no independent reviewer** (a cheap, contained slice; the mechanism mirrors Vitality Band, already reviewed). **Remaining on the row: Choice Belt** (sv02-176) — a TARGET-TYPE gate ("…Active Pokémon V"), a different shape (not a `BoardCondition`, so not this field), its own slice. *Why: the resume point named this "the last cheap D40 reader"; it is cheap precisely because the hard part (the condition vocabulary) already exists — the only new engineering is deciding where a seat-relative predicate gets evaluated within a seat-free aggregation pipeline, resolved by splitting aggregation (continuous.ts, unchanged responsibility) from evaluation (interpreter.ts, beside the one evaluator) rather than threading a seat through six call sites or duplicating `conditionHolds`.* (2026-07-27) |

# Decisions & Locked Assumptions

## Product / architecture decisions
| # | Decision | Choice |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Backend data strategy | Own DB — ingest tcgdex → Cloudflare D1, serve our own API |
| D2 | Accounts & persistence | Full accounts + auth; users own their decks |
| D2a | Auth methods | Email + password **and** social OAuth (Discord + Google) |
| D3 | Catalog scope | Full-history-capable schema, ingest SV-era first |
| D4 | Card images | Mirror into R2, serve from our domain |
| D5 | Card type | Unify — one canonical `Card`; builder/playmat are view projections |
| D6 | Online lobby server | In scope — real Durable Object (WebSocket) lobby |
| D7 | Game engine placement | Separate **`packages/engine`** (pure logic) — imported by both `apps/web` (local play) and `apps/api` (authoritative DO). *Why: the engine runs in two runtimes; an app can't import another app.* |
| D8 | Card-effect modeling | **Composable, data-driven op programs** over shared archetype templates (not per-card functions); engine emits **semantic events** consumed by the animation layer. *Why: cards are minor variations on a few archetypes; keeps authoring + animation cheap. Detail in `workstreams/simulator.md`.* |
| D9 | Image mirroring & ingest execution (refines D4/§3.4) | Images mirror into R2 **lazily** — a Worker route (`GET /assets/…`) serves from R2 and on miss fetches tcgdex origin, stores, streams; catalog rows keep tcgdex **origin** URLs. Card-data backfill runs as a **local Bun script** applying batched upsert SQL via `wrangler d1 execute`; a future cron does small in-Worker deltas only. *Why: a full SV backfill is ~10k images — over Worker subrequest limits in one shot and hours of CLI puts; cache-aside mirrors exactly what's viewed and stays within limits.* (2026-07-09) |
| D10 | M9 catalog search shape (refines D5/§6) | `CardBrief` **extended** with `types/hp/regulationMark/stage/trainerType/energyType` (card-table columns only — **no set join**, so no `setName`); `GET /cards` gains **repeatable `type`/`rarity`** (OR within a dimension) and **`sort=name\|hp-desc\|set`**; KV cache keys version-prefixed (`catalog:v2:`) so a shape change can't serve stale briefs. The builder consumes briefs through one adapter (`src/features/builder/catalog.ts` — accented `"Pokémon"`, stage/trainerType/energyType → the single `subtype`). *Why: the grid/filters/deck-math need those fields per tile; per-tile full-Card fetches or a fixture pool were the alternatives.* (2026-07-13) |
| D11 | M9 scope trims (pending P2) | **Kinds** (`subtypes`) filter stays a client-side per-page heuristic (server can't express OR across stage/trainerType; EX/Mega are name-regexes until structured data — P2 tasks 8-9). **Manual deck/folder reorder is session-only** (no position field in the schema — P2 task 17). **Folder delete keeps the lift-up UX client-side** (child PATCHes before DELETE) over the server's cascade semantics. **`RARITIES` is a hardcoded tcgdex vocabulary snapshot** in the rail. *Why: each would widen M9's already-large surface; all four are logged with their fixes in `workstreams/deck-builder.md`.* (2026-07-13) **Revised 2026-07-14 (P2-M1):** kinds now filter **server-side** (repeatable `stage`/`trainerType`/`energyType`) — only EX/Mega remain a client-side name-regex post-filter (tcgdex `suffix` not persisted; follow-up logged); hardcoded vocabularies replaced by **`GET /facets`**. Reorder (task 17) and lift-up remain as decided. **Revised again 2026-07-14 (task 17):** reorder is now persisted — see D13; only the lift-up trim still stands. |
| D12 | P2-M1 catalog surface & legality source of truth | `GET /cards` gains **repeatable `id`** (≤100, deck hydration in ONE call; chunked IN + in-memory ordering twin of the SQL sort), **`nameExact`** (case-insensitive whole-name equality), `serie`, `illustrator`, `text` (LIKE over ability/attack JSON), plus the kind params above; **`GET /facets`** serves the filter vocabularies (7 DISTINCTs, one db.batch, KV-cached). `CardBrief` += **`legal {standard,expanded}`**; KV namespace → **`catalog:v3:`**, with KV **bypassed** for >512-byte keys and any `?id=` request (per-deck id sets never recur — caching them is pure write waste). Web: **`Format.legalFlag`** keys BOTH the `legalOnly` filter (`legal=<flag>`) and `isLegalInFormat` (structured verdict beats printed mark; mark check only for legal-less fixtures) — one legality definition for grid + validator. Deck rules: **Radiant = 1 per deck total** (like ACE SPEC; official rule), Prism Star = 1 per name. *Why: filters needed server truth for correct totals; hydration was an N-request fan-out; legality had two disagreeing definitions.* (2026-07-14) |
| D13 | Manual-order persistence model (P2 task 17) | `position` INTEGER on `decks` and `folders` — **global per user, not per folder**: the web grid's flat array (position-ascending) IS the manual order, per-view filtering preserves relative order, and a nest move keeps the row's slot (folderId changes, position doesn't) — exactly the client's existing semantics. Creates take **min−1** (new rows prepend); migration 0003 backfills existing rows in the old name-order so nothing visibly moves. A reorder permutes the in-view rows **among their own slots' position values** (`applyReorder` returns the rewritten array + the changed `{id, position}` pairs) and persists via **`POST /decks/reorder` / `/folders/reorder`** — absolute assignments, ≤500 rows, applied atomically in one db.batch; unknown/foreign ids → 400 naming them; failure recovery is **resync**, not per-row rollback (the folder-delete precedent). Reorder deliberately does NOT bump `updated`. *Why: slot-permutation keeps payloads at the size of the move (not the scope), needs no renumbering pass ever, and one atomic endpoint beats N racing PATCHes.* (2026-07-14) |

| D14 | Engine core contract (P3-M1) | **`applyAction(state, action) → {ok:true, state, events} | {ok:false, error}`** — one reducer, never throws, never mutates. `GameState` is plain JSON (the mulberry32 `rngState` lives **inside** it, so same seed + same actions replay identically); card instances are **uids** (`"p1#0"`) over an injected `cardPool` carried in the state (keeps `applyAction` a pure 2-arg pair and snapshots self-contained). Seats **`p1`/`p2` are labels, not turn order** — the coin winner *chooses* first via an action, `firstPlayer` records it. **Choices are actions; mandatory steps auto-resolve** inside the reducer (mulligan redraws, prize setting, the turn-start draw), so a `Phase` exists only where a player owes a decision. **Events are the animation + wire contract** (semantic, serializable, payloads always copied — never aliasing state or the caller's action). **Wire-safety:** TS types are not input validation — P4 decodes actions from clients, so every index/seat/count an action carries is runtime-checked (three real card-destroying bugs came from exactly this: a JSON string `"1"` bench index). *Why: the engine runs in two runtimes (web local play + the authoritative DO), and an authoritative server needs a total, replayable, non-throwing function of (state, action).* (2026-07-14) |
| D15 | Mulligan compensation (rules correction) | Each player may draw 1 card **per opponent mulligan**, and **mulliganing yourself does not forfeit it** — so **both** seats can be owed at once (each off the other's count). `reference/ptcg-rules.md` §3.5 previously read "the non-mulliganing player", which the M1 engine implemented as an exemption that does not exist; the reference doc is corrected and the phase now carries a per-seat `owed`/`decided` map. The compensation draw is **clamped** so a player can never draw below the 6 cards they must still set aside as prizes. *Why: a wrong rule in the spec propagated straight into the engine — the reference doc is the source of truth and had to be fixed at the source.* (2026-07-14) |
| D16 | M2 staged turn tail, KO interrupts & damage modifiers (P3-M2) | The turn tail is a **`pending: PendingStage[]` queue** on `GameState`, drained by `advance()` (flow.ts): automatic stages run, decision stages either **park** (phase becomes the matching `ko:takePrizes`/`ko:promote` interrupt, prompt event emitted) or **auto-resolve** when only one legal resolution exists. `attack` seeds `takePrizes`+`promote` ahead of the shared `turnTail(seat)` triple. The parked phase mirrors `pending[0]` (dual encoding, kept deliberately for M2): handlers cross-check the two and reject with **`PHASE_DESYNC`** on mismatch. Win evaluation lives in ONE place — the shared `resolvePrizesAndResume`/`resolvePromotionAndResume` helpers used by both the action handlers and advance's auto-resolves. `gameOver` carries **`GameOutcome`** (`win {winner, reason}` \| `tie {reasons}`); sudden death is surfaced as `tie`, not played out. Printed weakness/resistance parse to a **`DamageModifier {op: multiply\|add\|subtract, amount}`** (×N / +N / −N; unknown garble keeps modern-era ×2/−30 defaults) applied weakness→resistance, floor 0 (§8.5); `DAMAGE_DEALT` carries the modifiers so animators can show the math. Data gaps never guess a KO: `hp ≤ 0` reads as the null data gap. *Why: KO resolution must pause mid-tail for player choices, M3's checkup KOs reuse the same interrupts, and additive legacy weakness ("+20", schema-documented) was being silently misread as ×2.* (2026-07-16) |
| D17 | Engine→playmat projection contract (P3) | **`projectGameState(state, viewerSeat) → GameProjection`** (`src/features/game/projection.ts`): `{ board, piles, pokemon, turn, activePlayer, waitingOn, pendingDecision, outcome }` — `board` is a drop-in playmat `BoardState` (`you` = viewer); the wrapper carries what BoardState can't (`piles` deckCount/discard, `pokemon` = per-uid `{damage, hp}`, `outcome` per-viewer win/tie). **`activePlayer` = turn owner; `waitingOn` = the seat that must act NOW** — the split exists because during `ko:promote` the actor is the NON-turn player (the KO'd defender), and a UI gating on turn ownership alone soft-locks. Hidden info is redacted structurally: opponent hand = positional backs (`opponent-hand-N`, no uids — a uid is stable across zones and would let a client track a hidden card), both prize piles = counts only, decks = counts. Public cards key off the engine **uid** so the Pixi layer animates a card as one object across projections. The phase mapping is an **exhaustive switch** (`satisfies never`) — a new engine phase is a compile error, not a silent guess. *Why: this is the same per-viewer filter P4's server will apply; building it client-side first pins the contract with tests.* (2026-07-16) **Revised 2026-07-17 (wire-up review):** during any `setup:*` phase the OPPONENT's active/bench also project as face-down backs (positional `-hidden` ids, no `pokemon` rows — a row would leak the uid key + printed HP); a hot-seat viewer flip at Ready was exposing the first player's face-down placements. Reveal re-keys positional→uid (remount, not flip) — the same trade as hand backs. |

| D18 | Local play page & engine card-pool sourcing (P3 wire-up) | **`/play`** is a hot-seat local match: `GamePage` owns `GameState` via `useLocalGame` (pure reducer over `applyAction`), renders `projectGameState` through the extracted presentational **`PlaymatView`** (the `/simulator` mock, retitled "Sandbox", is a thin wrapper driver), and the **viewer follows `waitingOn`** for the device flip. The engine `cardPool` is built client-side by **fanning out `GET /cards/:id`** (`src/features/game/cardPool.ts`, concurrency 8, module-level promise cache; 404s cache as stable `missing`, rejections self-evict) — NOT via the brief-returning batch route. *Why: `CardBrief` deliberately omits the combat blobs (attacks/weakness/retreat) the engine reads; the per-id route already serves the full canonical Card KV-cached, and this needed no api change while api deploys stay user-gated. A `?full` batch param is the logged follow-up to bundle with the next deploy.* (2026-07-17) |
| D19 | Drop-legality is a driver-supplied predicate (P3 wire-up review) | `AnimatedCardsLayer` takes an optional **`PlacementPredicate`** (defaults to the sandbox's `canPlace`, so the mock is untouched); `/play` supplies `gamePlacementPredicate(game, viewerSeat)` — a deliberately **coarse, gesture-class** gate (phase-aware: what CAN ever map to an action) kept in lockstep with `moveToAction` by a property test (every afforded drop translates to a non-null action). Fine-grained legality stays with `applyAction` + the error pill. Hand→hand reorder is rejected on /play (the engine owns hand order; affording it was a silent lie). *Why: the phase-unaware mock `canPlace` afforded gestures the engine could never accept (accept-animation → wrong-rule error pill), and M4 evolve/trainer drags can't be expressed through it — the seam had to move to the driver.* (2026-07-17) |

Web MED (found independently by both agents): the log row said only "put their hand … on the bottom", implying — against its sibling row — that Iono does NOT shuffle, so a player who had seen that hand would think the deck's tail was known → copy fixed to say both. LOWs applied: an Iono degenerate-deck test (deck shallower than the Prize count short-draws, does not deck out), the describe-title rename, and a real end-to-end log test pinning the 5-row grouped batch (the two-pass restructure was unpinned on the web side). Verified clean: card conservation over every degenerate zone combination on both sides, exact rng advance counts, "Iono itself is never bottomed", gate semantics (`every`/per-seat/opponent-prizes mutants all die), the projection leaking nothing (zero opponent uids serialized), no exhaustive-switch fall-through, HUD playability, and no demo regression. **Scope: the hand-refresh family is CLOSED** — the sv01–03 catalog has no Marnie. **Carried forward (pre-existing, not this slice):** every authored Supporter (Iono, Judge, Katy, Youngster, Professor's Research) has `legal_standard=0` in the local ingest, so they don't surface in the builder's default standard-legal search; and `GameLog` announces only the last entry to screen readers, so a 5-row batch is mostly silent. *Why: Iono is the highest-play-rate Supporter in the format and the last row of a family we had already built and vetted — it lands as three small riders on a reviewed op rather than a new mechanism, and the one structural change it forces (moves before draws) is provably behaviour-preserving for the four cards already on the op.* (2026-07-21) |

Both callers want exactly that, and neither wants the mid-turn KO sweep. (Houndoom sv01-034/sv03-133, Charcadet, Staraptor, Paldean Tauros, Dedenne ex ×2, Bombirdier) and "Discard all Energy from this Pokémon." (Pawmot ×2, Raichu ×2). Now the DO CONCEDES for the leaver first (a new private **`concedeSeat(snapshot, seat, now)`** — extracted from `forfeitAbandoned`, so the graceful leave and the 90s timeout are literally the same code path and produce the same `GameOutcome`, log row and overlay as a pressed Concede), and only then commits the lobby change. **The seat-keeping half is the real decision, and it answers the question 3c-iii deferred** ("does the leaver stay seated long enough for the other player to SEE the result?"): a new pure **`applyBye(snapshot, slot)`** (logic.ts) keeps the seat for BOTH slots while the lobby is in-game and falls back to the old free-the-guest / park-the-host semantics otherwise. Freeing the seat would have undone the concede a frame after it landed — same `abandonsMatch` → record-delete → blank board — so the concede would have been pointless. The cost is that a lobby which has been in-game has no way back to `selecting` except the host's kick — accepted, because **rematch** is the next slice and `endMatch` (D72) is already the primitive for it, and because "your board vanished" is a worse failure than "this room is finished". **Client:** the Back confirmation now tells the truth before it acts — `BackToMenu` takes an overridable `LeaveConfirmCopy` (default = the local /play wording, forwarded through `PlaymatView.leaveConfirm`) and the online match sets it to "Leaving forfeits the match — your opponent wins immediately." while the game is live, dropping to a plain goodbye once it is over. Silently converting "Back" into "you lose" was the one part of this change a player must never meet unannounced. 1835 → **1841** tests. `bun run check` green. **BROWSER-VERIFIED on two real clients, in BOTH directions** — necessary because the DO class has no tests at all (`applyBye` is unit-tested; the `bye` → `concedeSeat` wiring is not): the host leaving and the guest leaving each ended the match instantly for the player who stayed, who kept their board, got "You win! / The match was forfeited." and the `<winner> wins — the opponent forfeited` log row, and — the guest case, the void this closes — was never dropped to the "Waiting for an opponent" screen with the game gone. | D76 | The forfeit deadline lives on the SEAT, and the opponent can see it count down (P4 online, increment 3c-v) | 3c-ii could forfeit an abandoned player and 3c-iv made a graceful leave do it instantly, but the one path that still WAITS — an ungraceful drop (crash, killed tab, dead network) — waited in total silence: the player still there watched a motionless board for 90 seconds and was then handed a win with no explanation of what had just been decided. **The decision is where the deadline lives.** It moved out of the DO's own `ABANDON_KEY` storage list and onto **`PlayerState.forfeitAt`** in the lobby snapshot, which is a wire type — so the number the opponent's countdown renders is literally the number the alarm fires on, and the two cannot drift. The snapshot was the right carrier rather than the `match` frame for three converging reasons: the arming moment (a disconnect grace expiring in `alarm()`) already commits a snapshot and sends no match frame; a forfeit is lobby/transport state that the engine knows nothing about; and a reconnecting client gets it for free with the state it already receives. Mirroring it into the snapshot while `ABANDON_KEY` stayed authoritative was rejected outright — two sources for one deadline is exactly how a countdown ends up promising something the server won't do. **The invariant that makes it safe is `connected` ⇒ `forfeitAt === null`**, enforced by making `setSeatConnected` take the deadline as its final argument (defaulting to null, so you cannot write one without deciding the other) and by clearing it in `seatGuest` / `reseatHost` / `makePlayer` — the three ways a seat is marked present. That REPLACED D73's `clearDisconnectTimers`, whose whole reason for existing was the fear that a future branch would cancel one timer and leave the other armed: with the deadline on the seat, "mark them present" and "don't forfeit them" became a single indivisible write instead of two calls. `forfeitAbandoned` dissolved into the alarm, which now judges due deadlines on the FINAL snapshot and consumes them in the same commit. **A second, quieter decision: `readSnapshot`.** `SNAPSHOT_KEY` has no version gate, so adding a field would have made every in-flight lobby unreadable across the deploy; the snapshot is now read through a normalizer that fills fields added since it was written. That is the OPPOSITE of D72's answer for `MatchRecord`, deliberately: a lobby snapshot is a handful of scalars with no embedded engine state, so a missing field has exactly one sensible value and the cost of being wrong is cosmetic — whereas a `GameState` from a build whose rules moved reads back "fine" and plays wrong. The guard is on the field's TYPE, not on nullishness, because it feeds `Math.min` in the alarm scheduler and an `undefined` would set the next alarm to NaN. **Client:** a top-centre `OpponentAwayBanner` — "Opp disconnected — forfeits in 1:30", ticking; "forfeiting…" past zero rather than a frozen 0:00, because the server's alarm is what actually ends it and may be a moment behind; "waiting for them to reconnect…" when no clock is armed. Hidden once the game is over. 1841 → **1853** tests, `bun run check` green. **BROWSER-VERIFIED on two real clients, all three paths:** killing a client outright brought the banner up at +5s with a full 1:30, counted it down live, and fired the forfeit at zero ("You win! / The match was forfeited.") — which is also the proof that moving the deadline did not break the scheduling that D73 nearly shipped broken; and a genuine reconnect (same tab navigated away and back, so the playerId survived) cleared the banner at once and left the match running well past the original deadline, i.e. the returning player was NOT forfeited. Zero page errors. **The run also exposed a PRE-EXISTING gap, recorded not fixed:** a HALF-OPEN socket is invisible to the server — `setWebSocketAutoResponse` answers keepalives without waking the DO and nothing watches for pings that stop arriving, so a player whose network dies without a TCP close is never marked disconnected and never forfeits. Every ordinary way of leaving (tab close, browser kill, navigation, reload, crash) does produce a close event, which is why this has never bitten; closing it needs server-side liveness (a per-socket `lastSeen` instead of the auto-response, or an idle sweep) and is its own slice. *Why: a countdown is a promise about what the server will do, so it must read the server's own number — putting the deadline on the wire type that the alarm consults is the only shape where that is true by construction rather than by discipline. And folding the cancel into the same write as "they're back" turns the scariest failure mode here — forfeiting a player who returned — from a thing you have to remember into a thing you cannot express.* (2026-07-26) |

| D77 | Rematch is a lifecycle FRAME that ends the match and readies the asker (P4 online, increment 3c-vi) | The hole 3c-iv opened on purpose: since a mid-match `bye` keeps the seat, an in-game lobby had no route back to `selecting` except the host's kick, so two players who had just finished a game were forced to mint a new code to play again. **Three shapes were on the table, and the middle one won.** A mutual OFFER/ACCEPT handshake ("waiting for them to accept…") means a second piece of lobby state to persist, expire and reconcile, and a screen that can wedge if the answer never comes. A plain `endMatch` that drops both players on the versus screen to re-ready is correct but makes the asker press twice and records nothing about who asked. The shipped shape — **`endMatch` + ready the asker**, one commit — reuses the ready-up flow VERBATIM as the agreement mechanism: the countdown still starts only when both seats are ready, so pressing Rematch *is* an offer, readying *is* the acceptance, and un-readying on the versus screen *is* the withdrawal, all through machinery that already existed and is already tested. The pure helper is literally `applyIntent(endMatch(snapshot), slot, {type: "set-ready", ready: true})` — routing through `applyIntent` rather than writing `ready: true` keeps "you can't be ready without a deck" in one place, so a player whose saved deck vanished between games lands back un-readied instead of in an impossible state. **It is a `{kind: "rematch", from}` client FRAME, not a `LobbyIntent` member**, because its legality is not a property of the snapshot the shared reducer sees: only the DO can tell whether the match it holds has actually reached `gameOver`, and a rematch during a LIVE game must be refused (conceding is how you leave one of those).
